items.body:
Shangaan electro, amapiano & gqom fiends take note: Limpopo’s Serokolo 7 breaks thru with a thrilling introduction to Mapanta; a local, traditional sound he’s revived and modernised, somehow resembling amapiano’s taut log drum rhythms and tense atmospheres, but sped to 180BPM, spliced with toasters and FX bombast glittering with modernist melodic sheen. In other words: 100% zingers!

Repped by Björk during her DJ set at this year's Venice Biennale, Serokolo 7's debut is an idiosyncratic, adrenaline-filled reboot of South Africa's lesser-known mapanta sound, stirring its 180BPM rhythms with traces of footwork, gqom and hard techno. South Africa’s scene has perfused every nook of the global club movement for years at this point; whether it's the low 'n slow sound of Durban's gqom, Pretoria's kwaito-rooted Bacardi house or world-dominating log drum-laced amapiano, but head north to the country's border with Botswana, Zimbabwe and Mozambique, and you'll hear something completely different. In Ga Sekhukhune, a village in the Limpopo province, the Bapedi ethnic group have retained their own unique cultural form, mapanta, a "living communal practice" that has been maintained through weddings and youth gatherings over decades. Although its popularity waned after its peak in the 1980s, producer, DJ and sound-system operator Serokolo 7 has been instrumental in modernising the formula, sharing FL Studio tips and tricks and sound packs in the village to keep the music alive.

'Maramfa Musik Pro' is Serokolo 7's first widely-available set and is a great primer to his contemporary strain of mapanta, and although he augments the traditional rhythms with ideas he's skimmed from other interrelated rhythmic forms, the core elements still remain intact. The unique vocals, for example, are considered invocations, delivered in Sepedi, one of South Africa's 12 official languages. And they can't be cleaved from their ceremonial function, speaking directly to mapanta's importance as a community celebration, calling out to family lines and totems. The rhythms themselves, while similar in some ways to the brittle, high-speed work of Nozinja (who hailed from nearby Giyani), sound as if they've been marinated in their own juices, trance-inducing but simultaneously disrupted by Serokolo's unforgettable oddball production choices, whether it's field recordings, screwed voices or delirious sub-heavy basslines.

The album opens with 'Naba Ba Papedi', a bleak uptempo ritual that plays like an unwieldy fusion of gqom (that omnipresent synth drone), footwork (those unmissable rushing snares) and Shangaan Electro, with layered vocal chants and callouts filling in the gaps. Serokolo is a restless producer who's out on his own, something that only becomes fully evident as the set develops with the pneumatic 'Roskae', a fusion of vocal micro-edits and pressurised subs, or the electrifying 'Chunku Manabeng', that excites the core pulse with brain twisting polyrhythms and the occasional log drum smack for good measure. On ’Bonkoko Bagana' Serokolo lightens things up with chiming melodic hooks and a feathery manyalo-style beat. Unsurprisingly, it's this track that Björk made the focal point of her recent Venice appearance - a key cut from yet another truly eye-opening treasure from Nyege.

items._cn_summary: 南非林波波省塞库胡内村的巴佩迪族群保留了独特的马潘塔传统音乐，融合婚礼与青年聚会中的社区仪式，以塞佩迪语演唱，节奏达到180BPM。制作人Serokolo 7将这一濒临消亡的声音现代化，引入FL Studio制作技巧与采样包，使其在保留祭祀功能与人声召唤传统的同时，融入gqom的合成器轰鸣、footwork的急速军鼓和硬核techno的低频冲击。专辑中田野录音、变调人声与失重低音线交替出现，节奏如被自身汁液浸透般恍惚而致幻，既延续了Nozinja开创的高速南非电子脉络，又以独特的民俗根基和怪诞制作选择自成一格。这是该流派的首次广泛发行，为聆听全球俱乐部音乐版图中最少被触及的角落提供了一份完整的入门指南。

items.body:
One of the year's best rock records, hands down (even if it technically came out in 2024), Prostitute's debut is brutally smart, a fanged, radical noize opera for anyone who thought the Geese album was basically Coldplay with a lick of paint. RIYL Swans, YWHH Nailgun, Gila Band, Uniform. 

Since it was released at the end of last year, 'Attempted Martyr' has been almost impossible to acquire, with physical copies selling out as soon as they land in stores and the title track disappearing from streaming services without warning. Thankfully Mute has stepped in with a much-needed "official" edition and we can safely say it's worth the hype. If you're wondering where the anger is in contemporary rock music, Prostitute give you an answer within minutes, following a distorted, field-recorded prayer in Arabic with looped wailing flutes that are almost immediately disturbed by frontman Moe's manic vocals. "They come for me," he screams. "Be quiet or be killed, they said they'd come for me / Whose voice do they obey? Who sent these dogs for me?"

The band hail from Dearborn, Michigan, an Arab American stronghold that's been a target for the country's growing Islamophobia in recent years. And they assembled 'Attempted Martyr' during lockdown, imagining the plight of "a doomed zealot whose pursuit of holy vengeance spirals into a psychotic orgy of violence, greed, and lust." It's one of those rare records that sounds like a pressure cooker, actively replicating the anxiety of daily news updates that have rocked the Lebanese community to its core. References to classic hardcore, post-punk and industrial music trample over nods to classic Arab folk and North African blues, samples of Japanese experimental outfit Ground Zero's 'Consume Red' and lyrics that reference everything from pre-Islamic Meccan goddesses Allāt, Al-Uzza and Manāt (the infamous subjects of the Satanic Verses) to America's regular whirr of mass shootings.

The album would be notable enough if the music didn't live up to the attitude, but the five-piece are more than capable, backed up by Mdou Moctar producer Chris Koltay's dense production. If you've been as bored with contemporary rock offerings as we have, this'll restore yer faith in the genre. Heavy as fuck.
items._genre: post-punk / industrial / noise / hardcore / world fusion
items._cn_summary: 来自密歇根州迪尔伯恩的阿拉伯裔美国人乐队，专辑以疫情封锁期为背景，构想出一位走向毁灭的狂热圣战者形象，叙事涵盖伊斯兰前阿拉伯神话、黎巴嫩动荡与本土枪击议题。开场以阿拉伯语实地录音祷告起始，随后扭曲回授、循环哀号笛声与主唱近乎失控的嘶吼交叠，制造出高压锅般的焦虑质感。音乐层面将经典硬核、后朋克、工业碾核与北非蓝调、日本地下实验采样熔于一炉，层次厚重而侵略性极强。制作人曾与西非吉他手Mdou Moctar合作，录音密度扎实，使作品在政治表达与声音实验之间找到平衡，是近年当代摇滚中罕见的兼具愤怒与深度的作品。

items.body:
A mythical member of Turin's fertile avant underground, Filippo Testa finally gets his flowers on this breathtaking set of unreleased compositions that scrapes together vital experiments from discarded tapes and private archives. Genuinely shocking gear, ranging from spiritual instrumentals and electroacoustic inversions to labyrinthine synth melters - serious tip FFO Archives GRM, Keith Fullerton Whitman's Creel Pone sets or Buh Records' electroacoustic finds.

We're gonna level with you: we hadn't come across Testa before hearing 'Antologica 1977-1990'. But that's hardly surprising; although the composer had been an icon in Italy's legendary computer music and tape music circles, studying under Enore Zaffiri, the founder of Studio di Musica Elettronica di Torino (SMET), his output has remained almost impossible to track down. Eagle-eyed followers of avant excavation may have caught Die Schachtel's excellent SMET 6xLP boxset from a couple of years back, that collected head melting work from Tereza Rampazzi, Gruppo NPS, Mario Bertoncini, Zaffiri and others, but Testa was conspicuously absent. Now Turin's own Isotopes has done the hard graft, searching out remnants of his time on the ground, when he was presenting at local shows, researching alongside SMET and teaching, to compile a scrap book of his life as an artist that shows the breadth and breathlessness of his output.

We meet Testa in 1977 and 'Aethyr' is the ideal introduction. Performed by Circolo Toscanini, it's a percussive piece that structures bells and jerky piano phrases into almost gamelan-like jazz spiral, signalling Testa's pet obsessions: philosophy and spirituality. Slow, measured and meticulously composed, it doesn't feel overworked or hyper-academic either, playing like a levitational ritual or some long-lost transcendental minimalist side that might be shelved alongside Terry Riley or La Monte Young. The comparatively brief 'Parusia', a piece composed in 1978 for flute and two pianos, feels aesthetically very different while continuing to explore similar philosophical territory, overlapping different harmonies to create eerie dissonances and unfamiliar resonances. Working in the SMET lab, he created 'SER' with help from Zaffiri's electronic music class, juxtaposing his reverberating instrumentation with suspended drones and eldritch tonalities.

Throughout, Testa shows a unique ability to blend his spirited keyboard work, whether on piano or synth, with wildly divergent elements, sometimes orchestral (as on 'Minnedienst', for example) and sometimes deeply atmospheric. On 'Alba de Tormes', he plays against soprano Ellen Kappel's saintly tones, curling around her voice to functionally lift it out of the composition entirely, and on 'Floating World', Testa duets with Zaffiri, robotically altering almost-repeating phrases to muddy the timeline. Best of all though is the closer, 1987's 'Estatica, da Alba De Tormes', a piece that Testa performed on the legendary polyphonic analog synthesizer Voyetra-8, and one that connects a few dots, linking kosmische music, Fairlight experimentation and deep, spiritual new age without missing a beat. 

Huge recommendation.
items._genre: electroacoustic / avant-garde / tape music / experimental composition / minimalism
items._cn_summary: 意大利都灵作曲家Filippo Testa的遗作集，由Isototes厂牌从废弃磁带和私人档案中挖掘整理，收录1977至1990年间未发表的电子音乐与磁带音乐作品。Testa师从都灵电子音乐工作室创始人Enore Zaffiri，深耕意大利计算机音乐与磁带音乐领域。专辑横跨打击乐作曲、钢琴与长笛室内乐、回授式电子作品等多种形态，融合哲学与精神性主题，键盘演奏与电子处理、器乐原声与悬置音墙交织。部分作品与女高音Ellen Kappel及Zaffiri本人合作，探索重复短句的机械变奏与多声部模拟合成器的极限。乐评将其与GRM档案、Keith Fullerton Whitman的Creel Pone系列以及Buh Records的电声发掘并置，称其展现了从灵性器乐到迷宫式合成器的惊人广度。

items.body:
Long considered a diggers holy grail, 'African Skies' is a harp-led weightless jazz masterpiece from early Arkestra member and Chicago legend Kelan Phil Cohran - crucial, life affirming gear that’s compulsory listening for disciples of Sun Ra, Alice Coltrane, Dorothy Ashby, Chicago Underground.

In 1993, decades after his work with Sun Ra and long after he'd carved out a revered solo niche for himself with 'On the Beach' and 'Spanish Suite', Cohran was tapped by Chicago's Adler Planetarium to score a program they called African Skies - designed to reach out to the city's Black neighbourhoods and present the next generation with inspiration and education. Cohran was an obvious choice; he’d been working with young Chicago talent for years, opening the short-lived Afro-Arts Theatre in 1967 and running various educational initiatives for his community, teaching Black history and mentoring fresh talent.

The project aimed to present footage collected from observatories in Africa with music, tasking Cohran with recording suitably cosmic material for the score. Gathering collaborators Oscar Brown III (on string bass, piccolo bass and flute), Aquilla Sadalla (on bass clarinet, guitar, flute and vocals), Josefe Marie Verna (on harp, trombone and flute) and his son Malik Cohran (on guitar, string bass and flute), he set out to put together a kaleidoscopic soundtrack inspired by decades of research into devotional music, African history and archeo-astronomy.  The result is undoubtedly Cohran’s most ethereal suite, lifted to the heavens by his virtuosic performances on harp, trumpet, congas, violin uke, guitar, flute and his "space harp" the frankinphone -  an amplified lamellophone that Cohran designed after studying African instruments like the kalimba. 

Opening with the incendiary harp-led 'Theme', Cohran immediately hits the album's most-loved cue, the 10-minute devotional tour de fource 'White Nile'. Leading with harp, Cohran picks out stars from the wide, open skyline with notes that seem to ricochet off brown's basslines, while Sadalla's voice soars like a comet, heralding brass and woodwind flourishes in the track's jubilant second half. The record's flipside might be even more uplifting. On 'Sahara', each musician follows Cohran's jerky frankinphone phrasing as the band draw tight spirals that Cohran responds to with pitchy fiddle vamps. On 'Kalahari', each member of the quintet plays flute instinctively, coaxing out animalistic resonances, while 'Kilimanjaro' sends us off on a mutable rhythmic showpiece that's guided by the space harp's rhythmelodic clangs and clacks, forming a sturdy backbone for Sadalla's wordless scats.

A stunning set - finally available again for high definition consumption.
items._genre: spiritual jazz / avant-garde / world fusion / experimental
items._cn_summary: 芝加哥传奇人物Kelan Phil Cohran在1993年为Adler天文馆项目创作的配乐专辑，融合了非洲天文研究、灵性音乐与考古天文学的多重主题。Cohran自创的"frankinphone"（一种受非洲kalimba启发的放大版lamellophone）作为核心乐器贯穿始终，配合竖琴、小号、康加鼓等多种乐器，营造出空灵缥缈的宇宙氛围。专辑汇集了Oscar Brown III、Aquilla Sadalla等多位乐手，竖琴主导的引子后接10分钟灵性巨作《White Nile》，Sadalla的声乐如彗星般飞驰。《Sahara》以frankinphone的断续节奏为驱动，《Kalahari》五位乐手齐奏长笛营造动物般的回响，《Kilimanjaro》则以太空竖琴的节奏性敲击与Sadalla的无词吟唱收尾。这张被挖宝者奉为圣杯的杰作终于以高清格式重见天日，展现了Cohran作为Sun Ra早期成员与芝加哥地下音乐先驱的深厚造诣。

items.body:
Balinese gamelan master Dewa Alit's third Black Truffle outing, 'Baur Bentur' continues to shake up the formula like it's a margarita, placing Alit's Gamelan Salukat ensemble alongside virtuoso jazz pianist Sri Hanuraga.

With each of Alit's Black Truffle albums, his first releases outside of Indonesia, the performer, composer, instrument designer and bandleader has projected Balinese gamelan forms into bold new places. 2020's 'Genetic' set the scene, introducing his orchestra and his uniquely tuned scale and its follow-up, 2022's 'Chasing the Phantom' considered gamelan's immense influence on electronic music, centering some of Alit's most experimental material. On 'Baur Bentur', which means "mixing and smashing", Alit again looks at the push-and-pull between East and West, this time wondering how to work out a fusion that's progressive, not something formulated around the gaze of parasitic tourists. He invites Jakarta-born Hanuraga to help him realize this goal and its a sensible choice; considered one of Indonesia's most talented young pianists, Hanuraga understands both avant-garde jazz and traditional Indonesian music implicitly. 

His playing is measured but ornate on 'Sukat Tacara', played in fast flurries of notes that recall gamelan without mimicking the form. It allows Alit's ensemble to take a different approach, laying down hollow rhythms at first and slow chimes before speeding up into more traditional overlayed, lightning-fast tones in the middle section. And it's at this moment that Hanuraga really steps into the spotlight, playing jerky Thelonius Monk-style sequences that mutate seamlessly into cascading gamelan riffs. The title track on the flip takes a different approach again, integrating Hanuraga's piano more holistically into the ensemble, where it follows the gamelan's rhythmelodic thrust absolutely, adding emphasis, accent and intrigue to a sound that's already exceptionally singular.
items._cn_summary: 巴厘岛甘美兰大师Dewa Alit在Black Truffle厂牌发行的第三张专辑，延续其将传统甘美兰形式推向实验性疆域的路线。专辑以"混合与碰撞"为题，邀来雅加达出身的爵士钢琴家Sri Hanuraga合作，探讨东西方融合中如何超越迎合外来目光的刻板范式。Hanuraga的演奏节制而华丽，在'Sukat Tacara'中以快速音符流呼应甘美兰音色却不模仿其形，与乐队的中空节奏与慢速钟声交织后，在中段突然加速释放密集的传统层叠音色，钢琴随即切入类似Thelonious Monk的跳跃序列，与瀑布般倾泻的甘美兰乐句无缝互化。标题曲则将钢琴更整体地融入甘美兰的节奏旋律走向，以强调、重音与悬念为原本已极为独特的声音增添纵深。整张专辑在保留传统器乐美学的同时，以现代即兴语言与跨文化对话开辟出新的聆听路径。

items.body:
Oren Ambarchi's kraut-techno-free jazz magnum opus is back for its 10th anniversary -  an ambitious ensemble piece featuring an all-star list of players including Ricardo Villalobos, Keith Fullerton Whitman, Mark Fell, crys Cole, Will Guthrie, Arto Lindsay and Konrad Sprenger... Wooooo

You've got to admire Ambarchi's chutzpah here. 'Hubris' is an all you can eat buffet of his various musical cravings, a chance for his friends, influences and collaborators to flex a little and for Ambarchi to attempt to ride the groove like an experienced cowboy on an out-of-control bucking bronco. The first side is the biggest surprise, a dedication to Wang Chung's enduring, disco-influenced 'To Live and Die in L.A.' soundtrack that begins with ping-ponging guitar notes and Jim O'Rourke's synth blips, before elusive Berlin-based composer Konrad Sprenger (aka Joerg Hiller) drops in with some motorized guitar vamps. It's rhythmic gear that fits in with the Berlin school until Mark Fell appears in the final third with some typically fractured percussion.

On the flip, the groove loosens after a short guitar interlude. Ricardo Villalobos takes over with a suitably winding, minimal throb over live rhythms played by Joe Talia and Will Guthrie simultaneously as krautrock techno mutates into disco fusion. Keith Fullerton Whitman tries to nudge the track off the rails with his modular expositions, but the path is set - Arto Lindsay's axe is just the icing on the cake. By the end of the side, we're in full jazz-noise mode: everything's still pegged to Villalobos' central pulse, but that's the only element that's bolted down. 

Hard to believe it's 10 years already - we can't think of a better skeleton key to unlock the secrets behind Black Truffle's musical identity.
items._genre: experimental / krautrock-techno / free jazz / electronic fusion / improvisation
items._cn_summary: Oren Ambarchi 十周年再版的集大成之作，召集了 Ricardo Villalobos、Keith Fullerton Whitman、Mark Fell、Arto Lindsay、Konrad Sprenger 等横跨电子、即兴与噪音领域的音乐家共同参与。A 面以 Wang Chung 电影配乐为引子，吉他音点与合成器短波交织，逐步引入机械化吉他循环与破碎化打击节拍；B 面在吉他过渡段后转入 Villalobos 标志性的蜿蜒极简律动，两位鼓手同时铺设实况节奏骨架，模块合成器尝试将结构推向脱轨，Arto Lindsay 的吉他作为最终点缀。整张专辑以一条贯穿始终的脉冲为锚点，其余声部在其周围自由展开即兴与变形，从 Krautrock-Techno 经由迪斯科融合最终滑入爵士-噪音的混沌状态。作为 Black Truffle 厂牌美学取向的集中体现，这件作品既是各路合作者个人特质的展示窗口，也是 Ambarchi 本人在多种音乐语言间穿行的控制力证明。

items.body:
Their first project as a duo, 'Midmeste' is Aussie composer-performers and long time collaborators Judith Hamann and James Rushford's latest slow-mo meditation on musical history, psychoacoustic phenomena and minimalism, performed on cello and various pipe organs.

Hamann and Rushford have been working together for years, most visibly alongside Sam Dunscombe as Golden Fur, a chamber ensemble the friends established back in 2008. Each artist has moved decisively in the time since: Berlin-based Hamann outdid herself on last year's intimate and deeply personal 'Aunes', while Rushford brought his various experiments to a focal point on 'Turzets', balancing his tongue-in-cheek electroacoustic experiments with bold medieval deconstructions. Working as a duo, the pair isolate the similarities in their respective musical signatures; the title is a Middle English word meaning "the middlemost point" and signals the album's creation, where they searched out creative overlaps: xenharmonic tunings, organology, psychoacoustics and unintentional sounds, just for starters. And knowing each other so well is also a boon. Where so much minimal avant-garde gear can sound stuffy to the point of being exclusionary, 'Midmeste' sounds inviting even at its most uncompromising.

They use English early music composer John Dunstaple's 'O rosa bella' to anchor their experiments, returning to its core themes every time the album starts to veer too far off course. And there's a refreshing calmness to this technique; in the beginning, Hamann's piercing harmonics provide the edge, while Rushford's rounded organ chords welcome in a more familiar structure that Hamann respects with elegant cello tones. Interestingly, the duo were given the opportunity to record the world's oldest playable organ, a 15th century instrument at Basilica St Valere in Switzerland. Since they were both on residency at La Becque in Lake Geneva, it made perfect sense to document the organ's unique character and add it to their composition - contextually, it's right on point. Mid-way through the first side, we can hear its creaking, crackling wooden frame and whistling resonances, the puffing bellows and the sound of hands and feet on the instrument.

It's these impeccably captured peripheral sounds that give us a sense of place, bolstering the duo's engagement with history with a tangible historical object that still tells us its age. Tones warble, wobble and boom through the centuries-old pipes and Hamann follows the course with her patient, literate responses that add romance, mystery and humanity to what, on its own, might be dry. So we end up with forty minutes of some of the most unashamedly beautiful music either artist has put their name to yet - 'Midmeste' is a duet that whisks you through time, physical space and tonality itself. Remarkable stuff.
items._genre: experimental / contemporary classical / drone / minimalism / organ music
items._cn_summary: 这是Hamann与Rushford首次以双人组合形式发表的作品，以中世纪英国作曲家Dunstaple的'O rosa bella'为核心素材，围绕其旋律动机反复展开变奏与解构。整张专辑以大提琴与管风琴为主要乐器，特别值得一提的是他们在瑞士录制了世界上现存最古老的可演奏管风琴——十五世纪Basilica St Valere教堂的乐器。专辑中的环境声被纳入作品本身：木质结构的吱嘎声、气箱的呼吸、手脚操作琴键的声响，与琴管发出的嗡鸣交织。这种将历史乐器本体作为创作素材的方式，让作品同时承载音乐史与声音考古的维度。两位演奏者各自带来不同质地的声音——大提琴的尖锐泛音与管风琴的圆润和弦形成对话，在极度简约的框架内展现出精致的层次与情感深度。

items.body:
Field Records’ treasured Monolake reissue program yields a first vinyl cut of the influential project’s 2nd album - the last as a duo of Robert Henke & Gerhard Behles, before the latter turned attention wholly to developing Ableton Live software. Genuine landmark stuff for electronica fiends

In suit with the reissued ‘Hong Kong’ (1997) comp of early EPs for Chain Reaction, and the self-released debut LP ‘Gravity’ (2001), comes ‘Interstate’; one of Monolake’s most distinctive entries in the space where dub techno met concrète sound design and hypermodern electronica. The 65 minute album sees Henke & Behles ultimately conclude a vision of a semi-organic techno architecture that transcends club, home, and can listening, thanks to their judicious balance of whirring, syncopated grooves and custom-built, elemental sound design that feels remarkably future-proofed, then and now, 

In historic terms the duo follow a line of activated electronic systems from David Tudor to Lee “Scratch” Perry, Vince Clarke to Uwe Schmidt, Basic Channel and Autechre, by breathing vivid, imaginary life and space into circuitry and code. More specifically, in Monolake’s hands, everything teems with insectoid detail and a fascinating depth perception, conjuring immersive environments one can take as much pleasure from dancing to as simply admiring its elegantly awesome architexture. 

The relatively new freedoms of Max/MSP software and the pair’s ever heightened proprioception allowed them to enact forms of impossible physics that dance into hyperspace between the air-stepping lushness of ‘abundance’ and needlepoint D&B abstractions ‘ginza’ or ‘terminal’, showcasing sheer, advanced tekkerz on ‘gecko’ and serving the ‘floor with nexx-level depths on two parts of ‘tangent’, plus the metallic electro ping-pong of ‘perpetuum’ and 10 mins of proto-virtual reality in ‘amazon.’
items._genre: dub techno / electronic / sound design / IDM
items._cn_summary: Monolake第二张专辑《Interstate》由Robert Henke与Gerhard Behles合作完成，是该项目的收官之作。专辑在dub techno的骨架上融入了具体音乐的声音设计手法与超现代电子语汇，六十五分钟的篇幅展现了半有机化的电子架构，超越了俱乐部、居家与罐头聆听的界限。Max/MSP软件赋予的创作自由度使二人得以实现超越物理法则的声响形态：从丰沛的ambient lush到碎拍化的鼓打贝斯抽象，从金属感的electro ping-pong到十分钟的proto-virtual reality长篇构建。作品中充满昆虫般的微观细节与纵深感，电路与代码被赋予鲜活的生命力与空间维度，是电子音乐史上承前启后的标志性作品。

items.body: There is improvised music that grabs you right by the guts, the connection to this music is immediate and direct. Often you can feel it; it sweeps you away, strikes right to the core, and is able to lift you into a different state of consciousness. Peter Brötzmann and Joe McPhee, might come to the mind, Matana Roberts and Mette Rasmussen represent a younger generation. But there’s also music that takes a more intellectual approach, it’s harder to access, more abstract, more conceptual. That doesn’t mean it can’t move you, though - it just does it on a different level. The classic example of this would certainly be Anthony Braxton. Christian Lillinger’s projects also work this way - and they do so in a thoroughly fascinating way, especially when it’s his Open Form for Society outfit. Lillinger describes the second album of his project as conceived, condensed chamber music - an exploration of sonic possibilities featuring a specially developed ensemble, which can be rightfully called a who’s who of modern European improvisers (plus an American one): Kaja Draksler (celesta, upright piano), Elias Stemeseder (harpsichord, synthesizer); Georg Vogel (claviton), Anna D’Errico and Cory Smythe (piano) make up the keyboard section, Robert Landfermann, Jonas Westergaard and Petter Eldh are on the basses, Christopher Dell is on vibraphone, and Lillinger himself is responsible for percussion and the composition of the music. Added to this are electronic and electroacoustic enhancements, conducted via metronome. Characteristic of this music are highly condensed conceptual structures and rhythmic polyphony, yet at the same time there’s a springy openness that makes it possible to appreciate this music even without prior knowledge of music theory. Spaces of freedom emerge every now and then, in which individual shaping and independent interpretative decisions become possible - and it’s precisely in these moments that the music happens to be more tangible and exciting. At the heart of the album is the 14-minute “Poliform” - OFFS II in a nutshell, so to speak. Driven by flickering percussion and bone-dry basslines, the keyboards duel and support one another, creating expansive textures, breaking them up with rapid runs, and ensuring that the focus is constantly changing. Space and time are permanently shifted; it often sounds as if a cassette was wobbling along in an old cassette player. This creates the impression of coexisting temporal structures and a multitude of perspectives; rhythmic and harmonic cells are analyzed as if under a magnifying glass, only to then rewind the composition and direct the gaze toward a larger whole. The music thus eludes immediate grasp because it undergoes maximum change through its minimal shifts. Free jazz clusters exist alongside airy, transparent passages; frantic drum patterns reminiscent of pinball machine sounds are attacked by heavy bass lines. Here and there, a swing passage flashes briefly; in various corners of the room, individual keyboard chords flare up, only to burn out again very quickly. One can hear this album as a musical inquiry into the relationship of time, a question once posed by Karl-Heinz Stockhausen and discussed here by Lillinger, but one can also simply enjoy tracks like “Topping Abnormal” for their unusual beauty, or the punk attitude of “Vector“. Another possibility is to explore the psychedelic side of “Setzung” or the heavy metal influences of “Plant.” For this album is, quite simply, a lot of fun. In contrast to the first release, where the separation in the studio was the focus, OFFS II is about the unity of a shared space. The recordings were made in the studios of Deutschlandfunk in Cologne and reflect a sonic live image in which the entire material (with only a few overdubs) resounds and lives in a single room. Open Form for Society II is available as a double album on vinyl, as a CD and as a download. You can listen to parts of it and buy it here . You can also watch a teaser of the recording sessions: Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook
items._genre: free jazz / avant-garde / chamber improvisation / electronic
items._cn_summary: 鼓手Christian Lillinger的Open Form for Society项目第二张专辑呈现了一种高度凝练的室内乐式即兴美学。十一位欧洲及美国顶尖即兴音乐家组成特殊编制，键盘声部涵盖钢琴、拨弦古钢琴、合成器与celesta，低音由三把贝斯构成，加上颤音琴与打击乐，并融入电子与电声元素。整张专辑建立在复杂的多层节奏与概念结构之上，密集的节奏多声部与跳动式的开放性并存，演奏者被赋予在结构性框架中进行自由诠释的空间。十四分钟的"Poliform"是专辑核心，在闪烁的打击乐与干硬的贝斯线条驱动下，键盘声部以对位与快速跑动形成不断变化的声音纹理，时间与空间持续位移，自由爵士的密集音块与透明透气的段落交替出现。

items.body:
Bundled with sonograms, soundtrack visualisations and film stills, Carsten Nicolai's latest Alva Noto deployment is a soundtrack to his short film about Japanese textiles that attempts to connect acoustic frequency patterns with traditional weaving techniques.

Believe it or not, but Nicolai's always been interested in weaving. He was born in Chemnitz, a city that was at the heart of the East German textile industry, and has amassed a collection of over 1,000 historical textile patterns. So he was the obvious choice to collaborate with Hoosoo, a gallery in Kyoto that's been producing textiles since the 17th century. The main piece featured here is the soundtrack from 'Wave Weave', a short video work that Nicolai directed to capture Hosoo's unique weaving process and magnify the loom's machinery, showing the "algorithms and temporality embedded in textiles." Funnily enough, the imagery isn't too far removed from patterns Nicolai has been toying with for decades: dense, complex matrices of lines and geometric shapes that he shadows with his suitably austere glitches and elegant tones. 

But this isn't a particularly gloomy offering; far from it, in fact. Nicolai is sentimental about the subject matter and meets the textiles with awe-inspiring swells and pads, adding faint, mechanical rhythms only when necessary. 'Sono Obi Landscape', meanwhile, was made by converting the musical portion into sonograms, then using those images to create textiles. We can hear the sound on this release (and spy the accompanying visual work) and it follows its predecessor nearly, decelerating the rhythms and bringing out some of the more atmospheric tonal qualities. Honestly, it's the closest Nicolai has ever sounded to Boards of Canada.
items._genre: glitch / ambient / electronic / sound art / experimental
items._cn_summary: Carsten Nicolai（Alva Noto）为日本京都百年纺织工坊Hosoo拍摄短片《Wave Weave》配乐，将声学频率模式与传统纺织编织技法相互转化。作品将音乐部分转换为声谱图，再由图像生成纺织图案，形成声音与视觉的双向映射。配乐延续其标志性的极简故障音色与几何线条美学，但基调并不阴暗：面对纺织这一主题，Nicolai以敬畏的姿态铺陈壮阔的音色层叠与氛围化的和声垫底，仅在必要时引入微弱的机械节奏。第二首曲目《Sono Obi Landscape》进一步放慢节奏，将声音转化为声谱图后再逆向生成音乐，呈现出比以往更接近Boards of Canada式的怀旧氛围质感。这是Nicolai首次将声音设计、纺织工艺与影像艺术融为一体的跨界尝试，附带声谱图、影像可视化与剧照作为视觉补充。

items.body: Giuseppe Verticchio already has a rich discography to his name, and earlier this year he added another remarkable work to it. The album consists of 14 tracks, all of which—except for the closing piece—previously appeared on various compilations released between 2017 and 2025. It has been described as perhaps his darkest work to date: a tunnel with no light at the end, reflecting the vision of a world that grows more decadent with each passing day. The selection of tracks is undeniably dark, but not exclusively so. A considerable degree of diversity can be found throughout the album, which is hardly surprising given that the material spans several years of creative output. Nimh moves effortlessly between pure Ambient, dark Ballad-like compositions, Cinematic soundscapes, and Experimental passages. The opening track even features harsh vocals. Giuseppe Verticchio remains closely connected to his guitar, coaxing from it sounds of pure melancholy while also creating dreamy atmospheres that perfectly complement the album’s Cinematic character. At the same time, a variety of noises, textures, and subtle sonic manipulations enrich the background. The final track, a previously unreleased composition, fits seamlessly within the album’s dimension. One moment, Nimh makes us drift weightlessly; the next, it leaves us unsettled and trembling. Giuseppe Verticchio is clearly far from finished and continues to surprise and captivate listeners with his unique musical vision and immersive sonic experiences. (Rating:7½). Listen to “Succumbing To The New Conquistadores”: https://nimh-music.bandcamp.com/track/succumbing-to-the-new-conquistadores
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了Verticchio在2017至2025年间发表于各合集中的13首作品，加上1首全新未发表曲目，构成他迄今最具黑暗气质的一张专辑。整体概念被描述为一条没有出口的隧道，映射世界日益堕落的图景。音乐在纯氛围、暗黑叙事曲、电影化音景与实验段落之间自由切换，开篇曲目甚至出现了粗粝的人声。吉他始终是核心乐器，既被用来榨取纯粹的忧郁音色，也用来编织与电影感相配的梦幻氛围，同时大量噪音、纹理与微妙的声学操控在背景中铺陈。专辑在失重的漂浮感和不安的震颤感之间不断转换，将多年的创作串联为一个连贯而层次丰富的整体。评论指出Verticchio仍处于活跃的创作状态，持续以独特的音乐视野和沉浸式声音体验吸引听众。

items.body:
Perfection from Tirzah once again with perhaps her most loosely structured and hard hitting album to date, as usual produced by Mica Levi, whose chaotic but deeply schooled energy elevates the material here to genuinely all-timer status, using weirdo reverb and doubled up vocal phasing to turn simple hooks into screwed and unforgettable earworms, surrounded by compressed, almost clipped rhythms (the same beat on every track 🤯) stretched over lilting piano motifs that’ll have u covered in goosebumps from seconds into the thing. You’ll likely then spend hours/days/weeks trying to figure out how such bare, seemingly throwaway components can add up to something so profoundly impactful and unforgettable, before remembering that some music is just inarguably, inexplicably, touched by genius. 

“trip9love…??? is the third album from Tirzah, produced by long-time musical collaborator Mica Levi.  It was written and recorded at both their homes and various corners of South East London and Kent. 

After several recording sessions over roughly a year, eventually the music suddenly came into a sound that they wanted to follow. The tracks were built using piano loops on top of one beat, distortion added, then romantic vocal toplines. Poems centre on themes of love, both real and imagined. The world the record finds space in is a lazy club fantasy zone.

The speed, the connection and similarity between all of the instrumentals led the record to feel like one song, a diary entry of a moment or a fascination with one sound that they felt was important to go with. The nature of trip9love…???‘s release reflects how it was made.”
items._genre: experimental pop / avant-garde electronic / art pop
items._cn_summary: Tirzah的第三张专辑延续了与长期合作者Mica Levi的制作搭档关系，以极为简约的素材构建出极具冲击力的声响世界。所有曲目共用一个底鼓节奏，在压缩到近乎截断的节拍上方叠加钢琴loop与失真人声，通过怪异的混响和双轨人声相位偏移将简单旋律转化为扭曲而难忘的听觉记忆。专辑在伦敦与肯特两地断断续续录制约一年，歌曲围绕真实的与想象的爱展开，呈现出一种慵懒的俱乐部幻境氛围。整体结构松散但内部高度统一，听感如同一首长歌或一段日记，记录了某个瞬间对某一种声音的沉迷与执着。

items.body:
The standout track from last year's sublime 'Στον Ελαιώνα / Ston Elaióna' gets the deluxe treatment here, not remixed (thank fuck) but replayed on piano, bass flute and Prophet synthesizer.

Bennett's been going from strength to strength over the last few years and, following a move to Athens, he released his tightest, most finely crafted set yet, a suite of seven compositions that reflected his continental shift. 'Sacred House', that references the building that housed the Oracle of Ancient Dodoni in Epirus, was the album's thematic (and literal) centerpiece, played on Yamaha DX7ii and following a stylistic thread we can trace right back to Bennett's milestone 'Music for Save Rooms'.

And he returns to the building for a spell on 'Sacred House (Versions)', bundling the softly-hued original with three very different renditions. 'Sacred House (Piano)' is most surprising, because it sounds as if Bennett has treated his instrument, allowing him to recreate the original track's xenharmonic scaling. The muted piano notes hang in the air almost; it's the same piece, undoubtedly, but sadder and far more isolated. And the same can't be said for 'Sacred House (Bass Flute)', where the warm tones unexpectedly much closer to the DX7ii's glassy chimes.

It's the 10-minute 'Sacred House (Prophet)' that should make the EP a must-buy though. Playing Dave Smith's iconic polyphonic analog synthesizer, Bennett speaks not only to ancient history but to electronic music's relatively recent past. The shrill sounds are so familiar, echoing through pop and the avant-garde, and work remarkably well, hitting those microtonal notes more confidently even than the humble DX7ii. Gorgeous, ecstatic music.
items._genre: experimental electronic / microtonal / ambient / modern composition
items._cn_summary: John Also Bennett 将去年专辑中的核心曲目《Sacred House》以三种不同乐器编制重新演绎。钢琴版本通过特殊处理再现原作的非十二平均律音阶，音色克制而孤寂；低音长笛版本出人意料地保留了原曲合成器般透明清亮的质感；Prophet 合成器版本以十分钟的篇幅展开最为丰富的层次，将古代历史意象与电子音乐传统相连接。整张作品以古希腊神殿为意象核心，结合微音程调律、模拟合成器音色探索与跨时代乐器对话，在极简架构中展现了对声音物质性的持续关注。

items.body:
Experimental dark folk group Brannten Schnüre's 2016 album, 'Geträumt hab ich vom Martinszug' back in print.

"Dich lieb ich, Erde! trauerst du doch mit mir! Und unsre Trauer wandelt wie Kinderschmerz In Schlummer sich und wie die Winde Flattern und flüstern im Saitenspiele

The third stanza of Friedrich Hölderlin’s poem ‘Dem sonnengott’ evokes a narrator who is tortured by Spleen until slumber makes his childlike gloom disappear with music. Although today’s readers might judge these nineteenth century musings of the Imagination as mere stylistic platitudes, they also still speak beyond the grave as universal truths. A mere two hundred years later similar anxieties and hopes are still channeled through various art forms, with changing success and reverberation. Brannten Schnüre are one of those neo-romantic music experimentalists who add to a long tradition of celebrating folk tale and exoticism. Their meticulously crafted loops, hesitant melodies and heavily nostalgic lyricism could easily be translated to what the late philosopher and music critic Mark Fisher called ‘hauntology’, a postmodern longing for a lost future. To describe the beauty of ‘Geträumt hab’ ich vom Martinszug’, however, the term seems somewhat dissatisfying. Romanticism is a hard nut to crack in the Anthropocene, and Brannten Schnüre’s realms of the cerebral are too deeply ingrained in a German tradition of story telling to define them within popular paradigm.

‘Geträumt hab’ ich vom Martinszug’ was recorded in 2014 in Würzburg and functions as the autumn part of the band’s seasonal cycle quadrilogy (the other segments being ‘Aprilnacht’ (SicSic), ‘Sommer im Pfirsichhain’ (Aguirre) and ‘Durch unser zugedecktes Tal’ (Youdonthavetocallitmusic)). It deals with the Saint Martin’s parade, a mostly European tradition to celebrate the medieval spirit of Saint Martin of Tours, friend of children and patron of the poor. Around 11 November children come out on the streets with lanterns and sing ancient songs in exchange for sweets. It’s a period of snugness and expectation, of yearning and dreaming, and therefore a consummate subject for the duo to scrutinize.

To the adult’s ear the dream of the Saint Martin’s parade isn’t all that consolatory. The dark and slow loops of Christian Schoppik rather sound like motifs for a welcome paralysis. Sometimes as a gentle backdrop for vocals by Katie Rich and Schoppik himself, the repetitive structures serve as tricksters that trade innocence for the uncanny. The dream becomes a fever dream which quickly absorbs the listener into a vacuum, an eternal post-panic attack semi-relief. Maybe that’s the amazing paradox of Brannten Schnüre. The space they occupy is never comforting – as if being locked up inside a Carl Grossberg painting – but it’s also a subliminal aural zone you do not want to leave. It’s music as being, as a stream, devoid of climax or catharsis. And because it is flux and being, and exists to be taken, it speaks in art’s purest form. ‘In place of a hermeneutics we need an erotics of art’ Susan Sontag famously concluded her essay ‘Against Interpretation’ with. Well, look no further …"
items._genre: experimental dark folk / neofolk / hauntology / ambient
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Brannten Schnüre的季节四部曲之秋章，2014年录制于维尔茨堡，2016年发行后再版。乐评以荷尔德林的诗句开篇，将作品置于浪漫主义与幽灵学的交汇点上审视。音乐以Christian Schoppik构建的黑暗缓慢循环loop为核心骨架，Katie Rich与Schoppik本人的人声在其上漂浮。这些重复结构并非背景，而是如同狡黠的精灵，将天真转化为诡异。圣马丁节游行的童年记忆被重塑为一场发烧梦——一种后恐慌发作式的半解脱真空状态。乐评指出其悖论所在：这个空间从不提供慰藉，却拥有一种深层吸引力，听者不愿离开。音乐如存在本身，如溪流，无高潮亦无净化，以最纯粹的艺术形态存在。整张专辑在德国民间叙事传统与后现代怀旧之间找到了独特的平衡。

Oh man this is just incredible; Oren Ambarchi cracks open the work of lesser-known guitar god (and notorious instrument builder) Hans Reichel, selecting solo recordings spanning 1973-1988 that highlight his innovative approach to the instrument. It honestly sounds like nothing else, but followers of work by Oren Ambarchi, Fred Frith, Henry Kaiser, Derek Bailey or Keith Rowe - this will do you in.

Best known these days as the location of Open Ground, the German club opened by Mark Ernestus with one of the world's best soundsystems, North Rhine-Westphalia's Wuppertal is also the hometown of Hans Reichel, an improv titan and "experimental luthier" who genuinely changed the way improvisers approached the guitar. Don't take our word for it, guitarist (and Black Truffle boss) Oren Ambarchi credits Reichel with shaping his philosophy, and now celebrates the pioneer with a groegously compiled anthology of 23 tracks from his vast (and fairly impenetrable) catalog. Many might be familiar with Reichel mostly for his inventions, particularly the daxophone, an experimental idiophone he created to mimic animal sounds that's become a Hollywood staple in recent years, but the fact that his own work hasn't been raked over makes 'Dalbergia Refusa' a vital missing link, shining a spotlight on his work as both a player, composer and luthier - and it is quite honestly one of the most crucial reissues we’ve heard in years.

Ambarchi first came in contact with Reichel's work when he heard 1987's 'Return of the Knödler show' on a Guitar Player magazine cover disc -  and it soon changed the way Ambarchi thought about the instrument, you can very clearly hear its impact on his early recordings - especially his milestone 'Grapes From The Estate'. So it's a fitting way for Ambarchi to open the compilation - particularly because keen-eared listeners might recognise it for another reason, it's the track that Daniel Lopatin samples (and croons over) on 'No Good', 'Garden of Delete's light-headed highlight. With that one out of the way, the rest of the tracks really display Reichel's range: his technical skills using extra strings, moveable pickups or extra bridges, and his compositional boldness, freely shifting from solo guitar to multiple instruments or from pick to hammer.

'Wenn Das Rohr Dommelt', the opening track from Reichel's first album, 1973's 'Wichlinghauser Blues', foregrounded one of the artist's oddest instruments - an 11-string zither-style device that used piano strings and was hammered, with a shot glass used as a slide. It's shockingly unique sound that established a benchmark for Reichel as he went on to pull from US and UK rock and folk he grew up with, like on 'The call (I)' from 1979's ace 'The Death of the Rate Bird Ymir' - you can hear those ideas chewed up through his unique methodology. The American primitive concepts that Fahey distributed to a network of his acolytes sound different here, trampled by Reichel and his "full fret guitar" but not lost entirely. Similarly, there's an echo of psychedelic rock on the closing track 'Heimkehr der Holzböcke', taken from a rare 7" released in 1975, that Reichel corrodes with his advanced techniques, overdubbing bird-like squeaks and dissonant, blues-y plods. 

Another utterly indispensable history lesson from Black Truffle, then.
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑由Oren Ambarchi精心策划，收录了Hans Reichel横跨1973至1988年的23首独奏录音，旨在让这位被低估的吉他革新者与实验制琴师重回视野。Reichel以自制的非常规乐器闻名，如十一弦琴、带有可移动拾音器的全品丝吉他以及模仿动物声音的daxophone等，这些发明彻底改变了即兴演奏者对吉他的理解方式。专辑呈现了他从美式原始吉他传统中汲取灵感、加以解构重塑的创作路径，在锤击与拨弦之间自由切换，技术手段与作曲胆识并重。作为小厂牌发行的再版项目，填补了Reichel作品长期缺乏系统梳理的空白，对当代实验音乐听众而言具有重要的参考价值。

items.body:
Rising star of the Bristol subterrain, Jen Hartley’s Yushh tweaks spines to crafty electro/broken beat, industrial dembow & downbeat permutations for Timedance FFO Objekt, Batu, Hesaitix...

Yushh’s 3rd solo EP - their first in 3 years - builds on five years of turns for Wisdom Teeth, and remixes of Orbital and James K, with whipsmart advancements on her fine wrought yet rugged offbeat sound. It’s front loaded with more uptempo chops in the double-dipped, mutant UKG torque of ‘Petty Vengeance’, thru the percolated garage-techno razz of ‘The OCC’ and wraithlike ‘Mos Def’, both demonstrating deft, whirring details under the hood, and strong feel for darker cyber-dubbed atmosphere. On the other hand, she’s also adroit at more pendulous variants of the dembow-dancehall virus, tucking the tresillo rhythm with steel-tipped industrial drums and nagging EBM style bassline in a mean title tune, and holding down the pressure with a proper, pendulous Bristol steez on ‘To Be Misled’.
items._genre: electro / broken beat / industrial dembow / EBM / bass music
items._cn_summary: Yushh（真名Jen Hartley）是布里斯托地下场景涌现的新锐制作人，这是她时隔三年的第三张个人EP，延续了此前在Wisdom Teeth等厂牌的五年积累以及为Orbital和James K所做的混音经验。作品将UK garage的双跳律动、突变式的techno节奏与dembow-dancehall的tresillo三连音切割法相融合，鼓组尖锐如钢钉，低频线偏向EBM工业质感。整张专辑前端集中收录节奏较快的曲目，从双倍渲染的突变UKG到幽灵般的dub氛围均有所呈现，后半段则进入更下沉、更具压迫感的Bristol式厚重律动。整体声音既精密又粗粝，在cyber-dub暗色调与舞池张力之间取得平衡，是当下布里斯托低音电子脉络中颇具个人辨识度的一张作品。

items.body:
The Jamaican icon's final project, 'Spatial, No Problem' took Lee "Scratch" Perry to Berlin in 2019, where he laid down a series of surreal improvisations alongside Jan St. Werner and Andi Toma's spiky electronics.

When Perry died in 2021, bands rushed to put out their collaborations with the octogenarian hero, each claiming they had his final session: was it New Age Doom's 'Lee "Scratch" Perry's Guide to the Universe' or Pete Harris and Fritz Caitlin's 'Mercy'? The real answer is that it was a project he'd made with Mouse on Mars just a couple of years earlier; St. Werner and Toma weren't quite sure how they'd made the cut (it could have been a label connection, or a prior collaboration with a friend of Perry's, they never found out) and when Perry showed up at their Paraverse studio they were in shock. "We hardly spoke about what we were doing," explains St. Werner. "We met and got going. He was laughing a lot and we laughed along. We also cooked and ate fish soup and papayas."

Perry sounds old on 'Spacial, No Problem", sure, but he sounds as eccentric as ever, free associating over Mouse On Mars's seemingly casual blend of dub, krautrock, spiritual jazz and punky noise. Maybe they were the ideal collaborators to see Perry off the earthly plane; it's not your average dub album, but Perry wasn't your average artist, either.
items._cn_summary: 这是牙买加传奇Lee "Scratch" Perry的遗作，2019年他在柏林与Mouse On Mars成员Jan St. Werner和Andi Toma合作完成。两位德国电子音乐人起初对Perry的到访感到震惊，双方几乎没有事先沟通便直接进入即兴状态，在笑声、炸鱼汤和木瓜中完成了这些作品。Perry的声音虽显老态，但自由联想的特质依然鲜明，在Mouse On Mars融合dub、krautrock、灵性爵士与朋克噪音的电子基底上漫游。这不是典型的dub专辑，但Perry从来不是典型的艺术家，这组跨界合作恰好为他提供了离开地球平面的理想载体。

items.body:
Brownswood mark 20 years in classic style with a glorious first studio fusion of London’s crackshot spiritual jazz unit, Your Brother’s Keeper & Gary Bartz, a storied jazz saxophonist who’s played with everyone from Miles Davis and Max Roach to Eric Dolphy.

Among the most impressive drops on Gilles Peterson and co.’s label in recent memory, ‘Where Rivers Meet’ is a cross-generational confluence of consummate players who bring something timeless yet fresh to the table. It’s all heavily absorbing stuff, and at best when they go soaring and deep, as in the genuinely stop-in-your-tracks centrepiece ‘Eclipse’, where Bartz smoulders and rises on a heart-in-mouth bed of lushly cinematic synths, evoking Alice Coltrane and Popol Vuh scoring a Michael Mann flick, before they knit in widescreen kosmiche plumes propelled by tightest drums in ‘Solar Flare’, and likewise prove equally adept at dialling it all down to a tense hush recalling the recent Garth Erasmus turn on the richly synaesthetic sensation of ‘Petrichor’. 

"Gary Bartz and Your Brother‘s Keeper present Where Rivers Meet, a deeply intuitive new studio album capturing a rare meeting between generations of jazz musicians. Released via Brownswood Recordings, as the label celebrates its 20th anniversary, the record brings together Bartz’s jazz lineage and a new collective emerging from London’s vibrant jazz scene. The result is music that unfolds with openness and intensity, guided by deep listening and collective improvisation."
items._genre: spiritual jazz / fusion / kosmische / contemporary jazz
items._cn_summary: 伦敦新锐精神爵士团体 Your Brother's Keeper 与传奇萨克斯演奏家 Gary Bartz 携手，在 Brownswood 厂牌二十周年之际呈现这张跨世代合作专辑。乐评重点提及核心曲目 'Eclipse'——Bartz 的演奏在电影感合成器织体中起伏，氛围令人联想到 Alice Coltrane 的灵性维度与 Popol Vuh 的宇宙感交融；'Solar Flare' 则以紧凑鼓点驱动宽广的 kosmische 音景展开。'Petrichor' 段落展示团体对张力与静默的精准掌控，呈现通感式的氛围质感。整张专辑强调深度聆听与集体即兴，融合老一辈爵士血脉与伦敦当代即兴场景的活力，是 Brownswood 近年发行中具有分量的作品。

Leave your consciousness at the door and enter the surreal, labyrinthine back rooms of ‘Mind Sink’, the 2nd solo album by an artist whose only other credits are on TRjjs ‘Music Compilation “12 Dances”’ and a split with Alexander Holm for Denmark’s Sensorisk Verden. If chill out rooms w
items.body:
Berlin’s inimitable Tax Free Records grip TRjj’s CPH spar, Economy of Meaning, for a session of free floating ambient architecture echoing Werkbund audities via the earliest work of Goodiepal, and Civilistjävel! 

Leave your consciousness at the door and enter the surreal, labyrinthine back rooms of ‘Mind Sink’, the 2nd solo album by an artist whose only other credits are on TRjjs ‘Music Compilation “12 Dances”’ and a split with Alexander Holm for Denmark’s Sensorisk Verden. If chill out rooms were still a thing, this record is precisely the sort of soothing enigma that we’d hope to escape to: a weightless drift between phantasmic bass tones and spangled melodies, strafing in/out of the box from Balearic emulation on ’sun, sand, sea’, to cavernous soft mallet exercise ‘ore’; sea-legged ambient of ‘voussoir’; glyding free flight in ‘gap’; and creaking evocations of Uli Rehberg mystery in ‘Dwell Scene’ or the oneiric dimensions of ‘layer reverse’ and ‘anterroom.’
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由丹麦艺术家TRjj制作，由柏林厂牌Tax Free Records发行，属于该厂牌冷门系列的一部分。作品构建了一套漂浮不定的环境声景，融合了贝尼亚库勒风格的低音线条与闪烁的旋律碎片，在巴利阿里式的阳光氛围与洞穴般的柔槌质感之间不断切换。整体编排像是在意识模糊状态下穿行的迷宫，从'gap'的自由滑翔到'layer reverse'的梦境维度，每首曲目都呈现出不同的空间纹理。录音方式偏向低保真但质感细腻，引用了Goodiepal早期作品与Civilistjävel!的审美脉络，强调听觉的沉浸感而非结构完整性。适合在深夜或独处时反复聆听，能感受到北欧地下实验场景对环境音乐边界的持续探索。

items.body:
Rachel Grimes and Jefre Cantu-Ledesma collaborator Christopher Tignor deploys an anti-AI statement with 'Bleeding Past the Edge', performing the album in real time to display his humanity.

It's too easy, we suppose, to create music that's an assemblage of layered parts, loops and samples - if we can do it relatively frictionlessly, then surely a computer can embark on the same painless journey, too. That's what drove Tignor to create his latest record, working in his small studio with custom software, his violin, some tuning forks and pedals. He wanted to create an "immersive, orchestral sound" live, with just a single performer, without relying on loops and backing tracks, so developed the system that's displayed here. Honestly, we probably wouldn't know unless you told us, but there's at least a refreshing looseness to the rhythms of Tignor's 'Shadow Purposes' tracks, once the fusty opener 'Weight of Words' is out of the way.
items._cn_summary: 专辑以反AI的姿态为核心概念，艺术家在小工作室中借助自制软件、小提琴、音叉和效果器，构建出管弦乐般沉浸式的声响层次。最关键的创作理念在于所有声音均由单人实时演奏完成，未依赖任何loop或预制音轨，以此强调作品背后的人性与即兴痕迹。评论指出，抛开首曲的拘谨，从《Shadow Purposes》系列开始，节奏中浮现出一种未经修饰的松弛感与生命力的涌动。这种以技术为手段、以人为本质的独奏实验，将古典语汇、电子手段与现场即兴融为一体，为当代器乐写作提供了颇具反思意味的样本。

items.body:
A new set of unreleased sessions from Sun Ra's prolific early 1970s period bundled with two '80s live jams, 'East Two +7' is one for fans of Ra's off-world electronic material - ie. his most vital shit.

Honestly, you'd win us over with the fifteen minute 'East Two' alone. The 15-minute track was recorded in Chicago's Streeterville Studios in 1972 and emerged during a fertile period for Ra, towards the end of his time on New York City's avant-garde circuit. That year he dubbed 'Space is the Place', 'Universe in Blue' and the Moog-augmented sidestep 'Discipline 27-II', and that was only the beginning. Ra and his collaborators spent two days in Streeterville and went deep; Ra played synth, Pat Patrick was on bass, Kwame Hadi played trumpet and John Gilmore handled the tenor horn. And Ra's contribution is subtle at first; he hangs back, playing dissonant, sci-fi tinged tones behind his bandmates' wilder, bendier solos before lurching forward, jamming out nasty organ runs and unhinged oscillations before the track grinds to a halt.

Elsewhere, there's the 1973 track 'In Tomorrow's Realm', where Ra plays against the Arkestra's Ronnie Boykins on bass and an unravelled version of 'Yesterdays' that was recently discovered on an unlabelled reel-to-reel tape, featuring Ra on the Yamaha YC-30 combo organ. Even the two live recordings, a version of the 'Omniverse' favorite 'The Place of Five Points' captured in Columbus, Ohio in 1985 and a 'Fate in a Pleasant Mood' pit dub from the Arkestra's 1984 tour through Egypt and Europe, are worth checking into.
items._cn_summary: 这张合集收录了Sun Ra七十年代初未发表的录音，并附加两段八十年代现场即兴。核心曲目《East Two》长达十五分钟，1972年在芝加哥Streeterville录音棚完成，Ra本人操控合成器，在Pat Patrick的低音、Kwame Hadi的小号和John Gilmore的次中音号之间游走，开篇以不协和的科幻音色铺垫，待同伴们完成更激烈的独奏后才猛然推进，用失控的管风琴音群和震荡波将段落引向终点。1973年的《In Tomorrow's Realm》和一段近期从无标签盘带上发现的《Yesterdays》新版同样收录其中。八十年代部分包括1985年在俄亥俄州哥伦布录制的《The Place of Five Points》，以及1984年埃及与欧洲巡演途中截取的《Fate in a Pleasant Mood》现场版，这些录音为这位先驱者不同阶段的创作脉络提供了新的素材。

items.album: Slot Machine Music, Vol. 1 & 2: Field Recordings from Middle American Casinos
items.excerpt:

Back in 2009, PAN released its fourth album, 'Kenrimono', a set of recordings made by Greek sound artist Ilios at Japanese pachinko halls. The sheer density of it was as shocking and as intense as anything the noise genre
items.body:
Adrian Rew's properly hypnotic cult classic 'Slot Machine Music' has finally been reissued and it sounds even more terrifying and prescient than it did back in 2013 at the height of the basement noise era. One of the best environmental recording records bar none - don't sleep.

Back in 2009, PAN released its fourth album, 'Kenrimono', a set of recordings made by Greek sound artist Ilios at Japanese pachinko halls. The sheer density of it was as shocking and as intense as anything the noise genre had to offer, packed out with whirring, crunching and chiming resonances that took you to the smokey epicenter of the Japanese gambling world. And when 'Slot Machine Music' arrived a few short years later we assumed the sound would be similar; we were wrong. Initially dropped via Rew's own Ergot Records on CDr before the great Aaron Dilloway stepped in to handle the vinyl edition on his own Hanson imprint, the album seemingly grew from the Midwestern noise petri dish - but it wasn't an exercise in aesthetic posturing, using the racket of the modern American casino to mimic the intensity of a Wolf Eyes set. Instead, Rew was drawn to the experience itself, that's been meticulously designed by malign forces to guide behavior: those trapped inside the casino's four walls are seduced into spending more, losing more and returning to do it all over again.

Rew didn't know much about the environment when he visited Cleveland's Horseshoe Casino for the first time in 2013 armed with an Olympus LS-11 recorder and a camera. And over four months, he developed a peculiar relationship with the culture, surreptitiously taping the soundscapes at various Midwestern locations - in Michigan, Indiana, Ohio and Illinois - while attempting not to lose too much cash in the process. And it's a warts-n-all set, with dialog snippets and outdoor ambiance giving us more than simply the dense mass of chimes and stings and themes that you'd hear on the casino floor itself. What Rew is able to do is create a snapshot of a time and place, capturing the sheer desolation of the casino experience and using it to drive a narrative that Robert Altman would be proud of. The first thing you notice is that each machine's sounds are in tune with the next; "game designers," explains Rew, "tune their machines to the key of C in order to optimize harmonic cohesion." So although Rew's recordings are full-bodied, they're never too chaotic or discordant. 

Indeed, if you check in for the entire record - 2013's iconic 'Slot Machine Music' and its 2014 sequel 'Slot Machine Music Vol. 2' - you'll be lulled into the same false sense of security that entrances casino regulars. It's almost like ambient music, packed out with tiny sonic details that some well-paid sound engineer-cum-neurologist worked for years to figure out. Guided meditation music? New age crypto-psychedelia? It's all here, packaged in neon-lit one-armed-bandits aimed to target the dopamine centers of aging boomers with money to burn. And the best thing about the recordings is that Rew keeps some of the chatter intact, so we can hear him tangling with casino security, or haggling with his slot machine neighbors over change. We can hear the cheers and claps as paltry sums are won while vast fortunes are lost. The best moment for us comes when Rew wanders outside Grand Victoria Casino in Elgin, Illinois at the dead of night, the crickets singing as the machines echo from behind grand double doors. A freight train rushes past and blots out any other sound, distorting the recording.

It's a good reminder that although you might be able to hide from reality inside the casino, the Midwest will inevitably confront you with its rusted truth.
items._genre: field recording / experimental / ambient / sound art
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由声音艺术家Adrian Rew于2013至2014年间在俄亥俄、密歇根、印第安纳、伊利诺伊等中西部赌场实地录制，使用Olympus LS-11录音机捕捉老虎机的嗡鸣声、提示音与环境对话。Rew将目光聚焦于赌场这一被精心设计以操控人类行为的空间，记录下游戏设计师将机器统一调至C大调以优化和声共鸣这一细节。整张作品并非简单堆砌噪音，而是呈现出一种诡异的和谐感与冥想质地，仿佛刻意构造的神经操控声景。录音涵盖了室内赌场声响与室外环境氛围，构成对美国中产阶级赌博文化的批判性听觉肖像。独立小厂牌Egot Records与Hanson先后发行，以环境录音介入实验音乐与声音艺术领域。

items.body:
Rattly, stripped-to-the-bone IDM gear that harks back to simpler times, BOT1500's second proper album is simple and elegant, more concerned with the emotional weight of its melodies than the complexity of its beats.

You might remember Shinichi Koboyashi's last BOT1500 album 'Surreal', that appeared back in 2022 on AD93's Lith Dolina sublabel. And since then he's been relentlessly prolific on his Bandcamp, issuing regular single track updates that chart his creative process. But 'The Black Sea' is his first longer set in a while, assembling a handful of tracks that highlight his recent interest in minimalism, emotion and dub production techniques. The familiar monosynth groans and dry, jazzy breaks on 'Abstract Springs' might resemble Squarepusher for a moment, but it's much chillier, sparser gear, with space around each element that softens the impact of the hyperactive edits. And on 'Shadows', that same mood pervades the track even when the beats have been silenced; Koboyashi gives just as much importance to his chiming analog synths, coaxing out fragile melodies that sound as if they've been plucked out of time.

And there's a precision to his programming that's immediately impressive. On 'XB 1', his soft focus glitches and woody hits graze the post-dubstep landscape but subtly reframe it, setting the meticulous rhythms against echoing single note sine hits and melancholy pads. And the track's sequel 'XB 2' is an even harder punch to the gut, with exquisite melodies and knife-edge drums that shuttle us right back to 1996 for a moment, an underground dominated by Clear Records, Spymania and Rephlex.
items._cn_summary: 这是BOT1500（小林真一）的第二张正式专辑，延续了其2022年在AD93旗下Lith Dolina子厂牌发行的前作《Surreal》的脉络。整张作品聚焦极简主义、情感表达与dub制作技法，而非碎拍复杂性。专辑中，颤抖的单音合成器与干涩的爵士碎拍交织，空间感被刻意拉大以柔化密集剪辑的冲击；'Shadows'一曲在节拍消失后仍以清脆的模拟合成器延续低沉吟唱。'XB 1'以柔焦故障音效与木质打击乐触碰后dubstep地形，'XB 2'则将旋律与刀锋般精准的鼓机编排并置，瞬间将听感拉回1996年Clear Records、Spymania与Rephlex主导的地下电子场景。编程的精确度是这张专辑的另一核心特质——每一颗音符的位置都经过审慎考量，整体呈现出冷峻、克制却饱含情感重量的声音美学。

items.body:
Heat Crimes’ exceptional mixtape series lands its third instalment, this time featuring a DJ from Brasilia of Lebanese heritage - DJ Patwa -  exploring Arabic influence on Brazilian baile, parading 70 minutes of upfront favela funk liberally spiced with Arabic vocal idents and licks. Crucial, contemporary aural anthropology from one of the world’s greatest underground labels, no less! Massive RIYL DJ K, Anderson Do Paraiso, xavisphone, Ramon Sucesso.

An utterly fascinating study in modern Brazilian baile culture and its historic providence, DJ Patwa’s ‘Harara Baile’ homes in on the way Arab culture contributes to the hugely distinct flavour of Brazilian ghetto dance music. On the most immediate level it serves combustible party fuel, but more intentionally speaks to a near millennia of Moorish influence on the Iberian peninsula, and the mass immigration of Syrians & Lebanese in the early C.20th, as well as the difficult histories of enslaved Muslim Africans absorbed into Brazilian culture. 

In sides centred on the sounds of ‘Harara’ (Arabic for “Heat”) from Rio, and São Paolo’s ‘Jara’im’ (“Crimes”), Arabic samples are severed from religious connotation and used for the aesthetic properties that also appeal to any non-arabic user. Yet it also represents ironic, counter-cultural snooks at US hegemony, as in the tunes of Baile da Arábia - a wing of criminal faction Comando Vermelho (or CV, as surveyed on Sublime Frequencies’ SF038 in 2007), who are titled for anti-imperialist sentiments shared with the Arab world  - and the use of handles such as MC Bin Laden (now MC Binn) or DJ Sorriso Talibã, or in the emergence of the Magrão beat sound, characterised in DJ Blakes’ ‘Magrão Arábico’, for example. 

‘Harara Baile’ is to be taken as raw, living, expressive cultural artefact that does not belong in a museum, but firmly on the ‘floor, at street raves, and booming from car boots. Lyrics about everyday favela life - sex, death, drugs, crime - can be heard to mirror gangster rap (if you understand Portuguese), but with their own accent and set to very particular rhythms on a ‘Harara’ half focussed on 150-180 BPM carioca heat from Rio, thru the more rudely psychoactive and distorted, staccato sound of modern-day São Paolo surveyed on its ‘Jara’im’ side. 

It’s all among the fiercest testaments to the game-changing modernism of Brazilian music in the 2020s, and thus acutely advised to lovers of new music who appreciate that little evolves in a vacuum or under conservative cultures - just look at so much staid Western dance music dominated by rote bores; it just doesn’t compare to the thrills of this stuff.
items._genre: baile funk / world fusion / global bass
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑聚焦巴西利亚黎巴嫩裔DJ Patwa的mixtape作品，探讨阿拉伯文化对巴西巴伊尔舞曲的深层影响。A面以'Harara'（阿拉伯语'热'）命名，收录里约热内卢150-180 BPM的卡里奥卡热曲；B面'Jara'im'（阿拉伯语'罪行'）呈现圣保罗更具迷幻与失真感的放克变体。阿拉伯人声采样被剥离宗教语境，仅作为美学素材使用，同时暗含对美帝国主义的反讽——如CV犯罪组织分支Baile da Arábia以反帝命名，MC Bin Laden等艺名亦承载类似立场。歌词触及性、毒品、犯罪等贫民窟日常议题，节奏与意象与美国匪帮说唱形成镜像但保持独立传统。整体作为活态文化文本呈现，拒绝博物馆化，强调其街头、车厢、舞池的现场生命力。

items.body:
Supremely heavyweight 3+ hours of Phill Niblock’s immense instrumental slabs  - essential listening for disciples of Éliane Radigue, Tony Conrad, Kevin Drumm, Sunn 0))), Eleh.

R.I.P

First presented in 2006, ‘Touch Three’ showcases 9 pieces, 3hr 33min of material recorded and processed by Niblock between 2003-2005. Aside to its ‘sax Mix’, all works were produced from the sound of one player, on one instrument, into a sole mic, whose recordings were edited of breathing spaces with a Powerbook G4 to leave only the natural decay and attack of their tones. All straightforward enough, but the results are powerfully transcendent, producing sustained microtones that uncannily resemble electronic sources yet are entirely acoustic in nature. 

In effect the works induce an acute sense of suspense on the cusp of calm and dread, favouring the sort of resonances that one recognises from the “real” world, although exaggerated. In the process his organised sounds connote the feel of horror films as much as the hypnagogia of riding heavy machinery such as a bus or more pertinently a motorbike, the latter of which, along with the music of Morton Feldman, initially inspired Niblock - a photographer and pioneering Intermedia artist by trade - to start arranging sound in the ‘70s.

It’s safe to say that Niblock’s music effortlessly aids one in achieving rarer states of mind. Given due attention (it more often demands, not requests it), it holds great potential to inspire sensations of synaesthesia and short circuit audio-visual, spatio-temporal perceptions like few others.
items._cn_summary: 这张合集收录了九首作品，总时长超过三个半小时，全部基于单一乐器、单一麦克风的原始录音，通过Powerbook G4剪辑去除呼吸间隙，仅保留音色的自然衰减与起音。所有作品均经过极致的微移调处理，使纯声学音源呈现出类似电子合成器的质感。专辑在平静与不安的临界点上构建持续的张力，音调缓慢演变、层层叠加，使聆听者进入类似催眠或跨感官联觉的意识状态。Niblock将摄影与跨媒体艺术的经验融入声音组织，其方法受费尔德曼与摩托车引擎声的启发。整体风格接近Radigue、Conrad、Sunn O)))一脉的极简长音传统，但坚持全声学手段，强调物理振动与空间感知的沉浸。

items.body:
MBM & Merzbow rattle out side-long collisions of breakbeats and jagged, atonal tumult playing to both artist’s signature styles, for the industrial diehards at Cold Spring...

"'Extinct' sees the duo take listeners on a transcendental journey, focusing on the dismantling of beat and structure and recycling the result through layers of beautifully crafted noise and feedback loops, giving birth to new rhythms buried deep in the dirt.

"We may not speak the same language, but in the vortex of sound, there's a raw, primal understanding that transcends words. Noise can be art, a visual representation could maybe be Jackson Pollock's No 5, a plexus of chaos redefining what music can and could be. Pushing boundaries with Masami wasn't just a musical adventure, it was a masterclass in sonic anarchy" (Jack Dangers, January 2024).

The 20 minute opener 'FLAKKA' takes constantly evolving breakbeats which are gradually broken down over time, driven through a filter of harsh noise, destroying the old to give birth to the new. Raw and unforgiving, the track is a behemoth that blends mutant forms of broken beats and hints of dub, creating rhythmic noise of the highest calibre in the process.

'Burner' takes the record to its ultimate conclusion, the initial drum beat broken down so that it is barely recognisable. Pulsating distortion and high end audio fragments bleed into each other as the track lumbers forth and destroys everything in its path before slowly unravelling, degrading and falling apart.

A harrowing yet somewhat cathartic trip through walls of harsh industrial noise and audio degradation, 'Extinct' is a masterful pairing of artists who have delivered something truly unique yet totally relevant. Don't sleep on this one! (Todd Robinson / Subunit)."
items._cn_summary: Meat Beat Manifesto与日本噪音传奇Merzbow合作专辑《Extinct》由Cold Spring厂牌发行，将碎拍节奏与极端噪音碰撞融合。开场曲《FLAKKA》时长二十分钟，断拍在硬噪滤镜下逐步解体，变异节奏与dub元素交织成极具张力的节奏噪音。终曲《Burner》将鼓机拆解至几近消失，脉冲失真与高频碎片在崩塌中缓慢瓦解。整张专辑呈现出对结构与节拍的解构过程，噪音层与反馈回路成为重组材料，创造出埋藏于混沌之中的新韵律。这是一次跨越电子工业与日本噪音美学的对话，将传统节奏元素通过极端化处理转化为具有原始力量的声音景观，对工业与实验噪音爱好者而言是一次完整的沉浸体验。

items.body: Looking at the two covers side by side, one cannot help but see a geometrical similarity. To the left is what appears to be a giant fin, tapering off to the bottom; to the right is a blue stream with a large tributary. To the left, blue fish swim like missiles; to the right a series of shapes, traveling in the same direction. One cannot tell if this is all intentional or the result of playing Ouisi, but once the similarities have been seen, they cannot be unseen. One might add that the white segments of the album on the right seem to form a smile or the outline of a cup, while the triangular shapes seem sheared from the shark on the left. In like manner, the sounds of these albums trigger the effects of pareidolia. Manja Ristić‘s Devet, available as a disc on Flung, explores the symbolism of the number nine using an architecture of field recordings and music; Manja Ristić & Mark Vernon‘s Volim Beograd, a USB drive and booklet on Kamizdat, collects found tapes and field recordings to create a collage of past lives. Devet is by nature a spiritual album; Volim Beograd is a channeling of spirits. “The Navagraha” refers to the nine deities and planets in Hinduism that influence human affairs. The track begins with a drone that disappears and reappears like a breath, the second time with water, imitating creation. These forces were with us at the beginning, and are with us still. The “Nine Sacred Mountains” of China, also known as the nine sacred summits, play a large role in Buddhism, an invitation to pilgrimage and communion with the divine. As the wind whips around the recording and footsteps become audible, one can imagine the laborious ascent, the striving for wisdom. Kind spirit birds offer encouragement. In the center, one can hear what sounds like a prayer wheel. Continuing the theme, the tarot card The Hermit (#9 in the Major Arcana) symbolizes self-examination on the way to spiritual enlightenment. The sonic field is hollowed out, redolent of solitude. Ristić blows lightly on a wind instrument. Rain falls and water flows in “Nine Waters of Mictlan,” which honors the nine aquatic trials souls must face in the Aztec underworld. If only these souls had the “Nawa Sanga” (short for the Dewata Nawa Sanga) of Bali: the guardian gods of directions! Spoken aloud in English, “Dewata” also serves as a play on words. The pace is calm, turning slowly from drone to ambient. Not everyone agrees that there are “9,999 rooms of the Forbidden City.” Estimates include 9371, 8707 and even the legendary 9999.5, but the symbolism of the legend is more important than the actual count. 9999 is the highest yang number, symbolizing the eternal, one short of perfection and thus suited for a divine emperor. In the track of the same name, one can hear the sounds of water and excavation, a hint of the ceramic, like an archeological dig. “Sedna” is not only a dwarf planet – an Earth-like “Planet Nine” in the Oort cloud – but the Arctic goddess of transformation and the sea. As the water rustles, one can imagine not only the Earth’s oceans, but a matching sea in the deep end of our solar system. “Oya,” the Yoruba goddess of wind, storms and change, continues the watery theme; after performing a sacrifice, she became the mother of nine. Finally, the “Nine Rivers of Xibalba” explores the Mayan underworld, whose trials mirror those of the Mictlan. Many of the supplicants who now walk these paths may have been caught on the tapes shared by Ristić and Vernon on Volim Beograd. The album begins with a “Love Message” that is offset by the 988 subtitle – in the United States, the national suicide hotline. Side A embraces recordings of a bicycle race in Serbia circa 2003: on the surface benign, undercut by haunting drones that reflect the conditions in the country at that time. But when the yelling begins, one is grateful not to know the language: the language of bullies, ugly and angry, a fierce indictment, painful for anyone versed in the local tongue. These voices still exist and are in many places even louder and bolder today. History is constantly being rewritten; unfortunately all too often by the victors, who do their best to erase crucial aspects of oppression and all opposing viewpoints. Ristić and Vernon’s sounds come from physical rummaging, a priceless unearthing of source material taken from dictaphones, answering machines and reel-to-reel. “Obsolete media” becomes crucial evidence. On “Napuštena pesma,” clanging bells join the sound of what may be water in a cave, a further parable. At the flea market, people sell because they have to sell, sometimes their own legacy. At other times, unbeknownst to them, they sell the last copies of people’s voices in existence. What if the song in the third minute of “Istoriju na bubanj ” is the only evidence a man had ever sung? When these sounds are lost, do the souls of those speaking disappear? An opera singer sings; a child plays contentedly; a friendly conversation unfolds. The marketplace itself had been bombed by the Nazis, iconic architecture destroyed. Volim Beograd (I Love Belgrade) rescues sounds from the rubble like survivors, continually rewinding and replaying. One can hear both trajectories at work: peace and violence, love and hate. The knowledge of history weighs the listener down; the evidence is here, but the lessons have not been learned. Even if Side B is more benign, Side A sticks in the heart like a splinter. The more one listens, the more one believes that these releases are meant to be played together. The covers call to each other; they invite eurekas of commonality. One recording exposes the sordid underbelly of humanity; the other recognizes its highest aspirations. There is always a choice, and each choice has a proven outcome. The final track of Violin Beograd is a song of hope, distorted and abraded, discarded and found: a bittersweet excavation, but an encouragement nonetheless. (Richard Allen)
items._cn_summary: 乐评以并置两张专辑封面的视觉相似性切入，进而引出声音层面的共通体验。Devet以田野录音与音乐构建出围绕数字九的象征体系，从印度教九曜、中国九座圣山、塔罗牌第九号隐者到阿兹特克冥界九水，逐一展开灵性叙事。声音手法包括持续低音的呼吸般起伏、风吹脚步的自然声景、轻微吹奏的气鸣乐器与水流挖掘的考古式质感。Volim Beograd则以收集的磁带与田野录音拼贴出对贝尔格莱德过去生活的通灵式呈现。前者偏向灵性冥想，后者侧重历史回声，两者在pareidolia的框架下形成关于感知与意义的对话。整体关注非主流小厂牌作品与跨文化象征体系，与实验及世界音乐取向高度契合。

items.body: “Wasteland” is the debut album by the French duo Buzzkill. The album is available in various formats through Manic Depression Records, as well as on cassette via Ganache Records. The first five tracks are an absolute delight for the ears. Buzzkill’s sound is best described as Cold-Wave infused with Electro, driven by deep, resonant bass lines and rhythms that surge forward like a relentless train. The production is dark and, in many ways, pleasingly raw. The electronic elements possess an irresistible charm and occasionally evoke memories of the brilliance of Kas Product. The female vocals sound wonderfully deep and cavernous. Even when the lyrics are not entirely intelligible, the French-language delivery adds an ethereal quality to the music although you’ll also notice tracks sung in English. The presence of a real bass guitar gives the songs additional depth and weight, making the overall atmosphere even darker and more captivating. Unfortunately, the album consists of only seven tracks, and the final two songs feel somewhat less inspired than what precedes them. However, everything that comes before is simply phenomenal. With “Wasteland”, Buzzkill delivers a sensational debut album that will be very difficult for lovers of Cold-Wave music to resist. (Rating:8½). Listen to “There Must Be A Place”: https://buzzkill-buzzkill.bandcamp.com/track/there-must-be-a-place
items._cn_summary: Buzzkill 是来自法国的二人组合，首张专辑《Wasteland》由独立厂牌 Manic Depression Records 发行。乐评指出前五首曲目表现出色，整体风格融合 Cold-Wave 与电子元素，深沉浑厚的贝斯线与推进力强劲的节奏构成了作品骨架。电子合成器部分质感粗粝而迷人，在某些段落让人联想到法国电子先驱 Kas Product。女声低沉且带有回响空旷感，法语演唱增添了飘渺氛围，英文曲目则穿插其中。真贝斯的加入让编曲层次更加厚重，强化了整体阴郁气质。制作上保留了地下场景特有的原始质感。不过乐评也提到后两首曲目略显疲软，未能维持前半段的灵感密度。

items.body:
Detroit’s leading astrofuturist goes all-in on with a 76 minute odyssey taking in his slinkiest variants of Afro-Latinate techno, spangled synth kaos, syncopated bleep fields, Sun Ra-esque space jazz and one of his most widescreen visions in ‘March of the Purple Orbs’, plus interplanetary steppas on ‘Terraform’ and ‘Circumstellar Debris’.

 

"To this day, Earthlings have managed to dodge some of nature's more dangerous extremities, massive volcanic eruptions, Earthquakes, solar burst that knocked out the Planet's entire electrical grid for 3 years, numerous plagues of disease, food and fresh water shortages, domestic and International Wars and many other life-changing operas, but for this event, what remains is a realization that has no remedy. The cause: Earth's physicality has changed. It is no longer favorable for living things.

It is the constant shifting of the planet's internal tectonic plates which has unfortunately produced an unexpected and impassable dilemma.

Because of the collisions, deep within the planet's core, the planet is now producing an extraordinary amount of sound that includes a specific harmonic frequency that erodes the natural senses of all life on Earth.

It is intensifying. It is intolerable and it is unlivable.

Yet, some humans prefer to stay, to "ride it out" like the Titanic captain going down with his ship. Some, in total disbelief as some have concluded it is the second coming of Jesus Christ. But for most, the decision is clear. To live another day, leaving is the only rational choice.

At an increasing rate, scientific research data shows that humans and most animals, excluding the Jellyfish will eventually lose the usage of hearing and are to greatly suffer from an array of other neurological and psychological effects. The sense of touch and taste, sleep depreciation, severe nerve damage, constant hallucinations. Everyone will lose many of their cognitive abilities within an estimated 12 months from now.

On this day and every 7 days afterwards until all registered passengers have departed, the first of a fleet of large numbers of massive size spacecraft carrying approximately 1 million humans per vessel will permanently leave Earth to begin the long and adventurous trek across outer space to a new home: Vega. This is not a precautionary tale as there is nothing to learn. Instead, a decision has been made and a Trip To Vega is the consequence.

- Jeff Mills"
items._genre: techno / experimental electronic / space music / afro-latin fusion / synth
items._cn_summary: 底特律电子先驱Jeff Mills以一张76分钟的概念专辑构建星际叙事：地球因地壳运动产生致命谐波频率，侵蚀一切生命感官，人类被迫乘巨型飞船撤离至织女星。音乐层面，专辑横跨Afro-Latin律动 techno、闪烁合成器混沌、错位bleep音场、Sun Ra式太空爵士，以及宽银幕式的'紫光行星行进曲'，并在'Terraform'与'Circumstellar Debris'中以星际dub techno步态推进。Mills将冷峻科幻寓言与多源电子美学编织为长篇太空奥德赛，概念文本与音乐结构并重，适合沉浸式聆听。

items.body:
Oren Ambarchi offers a necessary new vinyl edition of his 'Grapes From The Estate' classic on Black Truffle. Out of print on any format for years, it’s a pleasure to see and hear this new reissue in the flesh, and to be reminded of when its floating harmonic tones first deeply seduced us and our friends. True to say its lost none of its capacity to soothe and absorb listeners like few other records we can think of. A proper modern drone evergreen.

“Oren Ambarchi's third solo project for Touch [after Suspension and Insulation] sees him reaching beyond the work for electric guitar that he's become recognised for, expanding his palette and taking his investigations into another sphere entirely. Grapes from the Estate features new instrumentation (strings, tuned bells, percussion and others that can only be guessed at), but the singular and unmistakable influence that Ambarchi exerts on these new materials is what makes it such an indelible work. 

There is a reconciliation of his love of song-based music and his determination to deal in pure sound. The result is a work that truly eludes such arbitrary definitions. Grapes From The Estate is an all consuming experience that draws the listener out of an ordinary sense of time, into a world beyond it. 

On more than any other release, his entire body of work to date can be experienced in a single statement. There are the seemingly random tonal structures that are such a large part of his vocabulary, the playfulness and humour of his formative noise schooling, his love of free jazz, of pop music, and rhythmic elements, perhaps subconsciously derived from his Sephardic heritage. Another outpouring of personal, intimate and enduring music from Oren Ambarchi.”
items._genre: experimental / drone / contemporary composition / free jazz
items._cn_summary: Oren Ambarchi 重新发行其经典专辑《Grapes From The Estate》，由独立厂牌 Black Truffle 以黑胶形式再版。这张作品标志着艺术家从电吉他媒介扩展至弦乐、调谐钟、打击乐等多元乐器，但始终保持着鲜明的个人风格。专辑体现了旋律性音乐与纯粹声响之间的融合——音调结构看似随机却暗藏逻辑，早期噪音训练中的幽默感、自由爵士的影响、流行音乐元素以及源自其塞法迪犹太传统的节奏特征交织在一起。整张专辑营造出超越日常时间感知的沉浸式听觉体验，漂浮的和声音调具有极强的吸收力，使听众完全沉入其声场之中。评论将其定位为现代 drone 音乐的常青之作，融合了个人化、亲密化的创作语汇。
