items.body:
Nurse With Wound's sleaziest groovers are treated to 30+ year VIP reworks by Andrew Liles, Matthew Waldron (err.app. (ext)), Diarmuid MacDiarmada, and Jean-Jacques Birgé.

A fan fave since its ’94 release, the OG ‘Rock ’N’ Roll Station’ framed Steven Stapleton, Colin Potter and co. indulging, to-the-hilt, a sherm-huffing type of low down swagger surely indebted to Captain Beefheart as much as Jacques Berrocal. Its status as a proper NWW classic has been cemented over the decades, and now returns glazed with mucky moxie by key co-conspirators.

Sometime band member Matthew Waldron emphasises the grinding title tune’s blues roots with modal psych guitar and layers of squirming vox on the Gros Module version, while Dublin linchpin Diarmaid MacDiarmada condenses the fumes of ‘Finsbury Park, May 8th, 1 35pm (Worlds to Conquer)’ in an illicit workshop of cranky clangs and atmospheric enigma.

Key NWW figure Andrew Liles hews closer to the original industrial swag of the title tune, extending and smearing its brothel creep in deeply trippy ‘Strange Wax’ alternative, and French composer-film director Jean-Jacques Birgé rudely distends and kneads ‘A Silhouette & A Thumback (Dance in Hyperspace)’ to a disfigured crumple laced with lysergic potency.

Ace!
items._cn_summary: Nurse With Wound经典专辑《Rock 'N' Roll Redux》迎来四位合作者的重新解构。Andrew Liles延续原作工业气质，将标题曲拉伸为迷幻的'Strange Wax'变奏；Matthew Waldron以模态迷幻吉他和人声层堆叠强化蓝调根源；都柏林音乐人Diarmuid MacDiarmada在铿锵撞击声与氛围谜团中凝练原作烟雾感；法国作曲家Jean-Jacques Birgé则将曲目揉捏成迷幻扭曲的残骸形态。整体再版保留了原始作品的肮脏低俗气息与工业棱角，同时通过不同创作者的视角拓展了声音探索的边界，是Nurse With Wound粉丝和实验音乐爱好者值得关注的remix合集。

items.body:
Brannten Schnüre, the experimental dark folk group out of Würzburg, Germany's 2015 album, 'Sommer Im Pfirsichhain' back in print.

"Christian Schoppik composed and played all the music, Katie Rich whispers, recites and sings. Together they make astoundingly beautiful folk with a rich instrumentation leaning towards the atonal spectrum. Instrumental wanderings stand alongside Nico-esque poetry tales. Christian plays the accordeon and in some songs guitar and flute. Inspired by hierophants like Nový Svět and David Jackman, solemn song fragments (a lot of old greek rembetiko-recordings) are modified and looped, with additional instruments and voices being integrated later on. His music has been described as “surreal folkcollage” and “german hauntology”.

With the emergence of Schoppik’s second project, a dada cabaret called Agnes Beil in 2010, Brannten Schnüre moved closer to the song structures of its frivolous sibling. The songs of Schoppik’s latest creation Sommer im Pfirsichhain are further accompanied by a female singing voice, lending the pieces the voluptuous quality of a stickily tense midsummer. Sommer Im Pfirschhain (Summer In The Peachgrove) is the second part of a quartet of releases. The first being Aprilnacht which got released on Sic Sic Tapes last year. Part three Geträumt hab' ich vom Martinszug and part four will follow later.

Reference points are bands like Winter Family and Twinsistermoon. Music etched on folkloric, ritual elements transferred into the 21th century. Also worth mentioning is the hand-drawn artwork which is made by artist Gwénola Carrère."
items._genre: experimental dark folk / hauntology / surreal folk collage
items._cn_summary: Brannten Schnüre 来自德国维尔茨堡，2015年的专辑以黑胶再版形式回归。整张作品由Christian Schoppik一人作曲并演奏手风琴、吉他与长笛，Katie Rich以低语、念白与演唱交织其间。音乐根植于民谣骨架，却向无调性领域延展，乐器漫游段落与Nico式的诗性叙事并存。制作上借鉴古希腊rembetiko录音素材，对其进行循环、变形与分层处理，被评论者形容为"超现实民谣拼贴"与"德国幽灵学"。专辑旋律呈现出仲夏般黏稠而紧张的质感，女声入歌后更显丰盈。乐评将其与Nový Svět、David Jackman、Winter Family、Twinsistermoon并列参考，强调其将民俗仪式元素转化至二十一世纪语境的艺术意图。

items.body:
Mika Vainio & Ilpo Väisänen’s prodigious 1st mission as Panasonic, originally issued in 1994, before the A went AWOL.

A real slice of history right here, presenting longer and harder versions of a cut that appeared in a shorter form on Mika’s Ø album ‘Metri’, co-credited to him and Ilpo, and here going longer and doubled up with another duo battering ram, ‘Murtaja’. Both tunes sound very much of their time, when European techno was forged tougher to demand, paralleling movements of harder Chicago house and Detroit warehouse techno.

In Panasonic’s case, the results were typically ascetic, mostly bleached of discernible melody beyond rhythmelodic cadence, and locked, bloody-minded, to icy tattoos that reflected their originals in Finnish warehouse parties, and would pin them on the international techno and electronic music maps. Trust that ‘Muuntaja’ still leaves welts from its distorted kicks, and contains subs primed to quake foundations, whilst the B-side is ideal for gnashing rave punks and bass drum fetishists.
items._cn_summary: Panasonic（芬兰电子音乐先驱Mika Vainio与Ilpo Väisänen的合作项目）1994年发行的首张作品，展现了早期欧洲硬质techno的原初面貌。专辑收录了两首加长版本的硬核舞曲曲目，节奏冷酷、几乎剥除旋律，仅保留节奏律动作为骨架。失真的底鼓与次低频冲击构成主要声响，灵感源自芬兰仓库派对的严酷环境，将芝加哥硬派house与底特律仓库techno的硬度进一步推向极端。A面以扭曲踢鼓和地震般的次低频为特征，B面则更适合锐舞场景与低音鼓爱好者。作为芬兰地下电子场景的历史性文献，这张作品记录了欧洲techno走向工业级硬度的关键时刻，具有重要的档案价值与场景意义。

items.body:
On a lushly poised suite of synth-gilded fusions with santur string virtuosos, Ustad Nawab Khan & Naved Nawab Khan, Catalan shapeshifter Pedro Vian refers to the inventive Indian electronics of The NID tapes, via Ravi Shankar & Philip Glass duos, or new age trips of Ariel Kalma

"Recorded during an intense week of sessions at Pedro Vian’s studio in Barcelona, the album captures a rare and concentrated encounter between traditions, generations, and sonic languages.

Ustad Nawab Khan, a 9th-generation master of the santoor and founder of Raaga Science, has devoted his life to exploring the emotional and psychological dimensions of Indian raaga music. His philosophy, “Raag se Ras utpan” — the creation of emotional states through specific raagas — forms a conceptual backbone for the project. Carrying the lineage forward, Naved Nawab Khan represents the 10th generation, bringing a contemporary global awareness while remaining deeply rooted in classical tradition.

The Bubble of Love unfolds through four meditations that create a dialogue between ancient tonal systems and modern electronic exploration. In three of the four pieces, the chromatic subtleties and traditional scales of the santoor intertwine with Pedro Vian’s unexpected synthesizers and electronic textures. These compositions form a bridge between Occidental and Oriental musical worlds, where resonance becomes a shared language.

In the fourth and final meditation, the collaboration shifts toward a more experimental dimension. While maintaining the same instrumental foundation — santoor and electronics — Pedro Vian explores alternative notes and scale structures, expanding the harmonic field. This movement reflects both understanding and incomprehension, alignment and tension between cultures. Rather than resolving differences, the music inhabits them, transforming contrast into a space of discovery.

Released on Modern Obscure Music, The Bubble of Love is not merely a fusion record. It is a concentrated meeting point — lineage and futurism, discipline and experimentation — crystallized in a week of deep listening and creative exchange within an intimate studio environment. At moments, the record subtly echoes earlier attempts to translate ancient traditions through emerging technologies. It recalls the spirit of experimentation found in projects where Moog synthesis sought to interpret the tonal worlds of classical instruments — from the dialogues between Ravi Shankar and Philip Glass, to the exploratory journeys of Ariel Kalma, whose music continues to resonate powerfully in the very walls where this album was recorded.

In this broader historical context, The Bubble of Love also resonates with the pioneering electronic explorations documented in The NID Tapes — the collection of early Indian electronic works recorded between 1969 and 1972 at the National Institute of Design in Ahmedabad. Founded with the support of composer David Tudor, who installed a Moog modular system in 1969, the NID studio became a radical space of post-independence experimentation, where composers such as Gita Sarabhai, I.S. Mathur, Atul Desai, S.C. Sharma and Jinraj Joshipura explored analogue synthesis, tape collage, voice and field recording — forging a meeting point between Western and Indian avant-garde traditions. Uncovered and restored through the long-term research of British artist Paul Purgas, and later presented alongside the publication Subcontinental Synthesis: Electronic Music at the National Institute of Design, India 1969–1972, The NID Tapes revealed a visionary chapter in South Asia’s sonic imagination — one where electronic instruments did not replace tradition, but refracted it into new forms.

While separated by decades and geography, The Bubble of Love inhabits a similar philosophical terrain: not the fusion of opposites, but the coexistence of lineages — where electronic sound becomes not an imposition, but a listening device. A way of approaching tradition with curiosity rather than control. In this sense, the album stands both as a continuation and a renewal — a contemporary meditation on the enduring dialogue between heritage and experimentation, between memory and future sound."

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是加泰罗尼亚电子音乐人Pedro Vian与印度桑图尔琴大师Ustad Nawab Khan及其子Naved Nawab Khan在巴塞罗那工作室一周密集录制的成果。四段冥想式作品在桑图尔琴传统音阶与电子合成器之间建立对话，前三首以桑图尔的半音微妙与合成器质感交织，搭建东西方声学桥梁；第四首转向实验性方向，Vian探索替代音阶与和声结构，让文化间的理解与隔阂并存，将差异转化为发现空间。专辑以Raag se Ras（通过特定拉格创造情感状态）为概念核心，将印度古典传承与电子实验融合，延续了NID磁带、Ravi Shankar与Philip Glass合作及Ariel Kalma新时代的探索脉络。发行于独立小厂牌Modern Obscure Music，是一次代际传承与未来主义、纪律与实验并存的深度创作交汇。

items.body:
Verve Vault re-issue Coltrane's 1966 LP 'Ascension'.

"Ascension, released in 1966 on Impulse! Records, stands as one of John Coltrane’s most radical and influential works. Subtitled “Edition I & II” to reflect the two complete takes recorded at the session—and presented together on LP for the first time—the piece is a nearly 40-minute large-ensemble performance marking Coltrane’s decisive embrace of the avant-garde. Recorded on June 28, 1965, at Rudy Van Gelder’s Englewood Cliffs studio and produced by Bob Thiele, the session assembled an expanded ensemble of eleven musicians. Alongside Coltrane’s tenor saxophone are trumpeters Freddie Hubbard and Dewey Johnson; saxophonists Pharoah Sanders, Marion Brown, John Tchicai, and Archie Shepp; pianist McCoy Tyner; bassists Art Davis and Jimmy Garrison; and drummer Elvin Jones. The music alternates between densely textured collective improvisation and extended solo statements, conjuring a hurricane of violent, searching sound. Initially controversial for its intensity and freedom, Ascension has since come to be recognized as a landmark of modern jazz and a defining statement of the emerging free-jazz movement. Presenting both takes together highlights the organic, ever-changing character of the performance and affirms its enduring place in Coltrane’s artistic legacy."
items._genre: free jazz / avant-garde / large ensemble improvisation
items._cn_summary: 约翰·科尔曼1965年6月在Rudy Van Gelder工作室录制的这张专辑是一次大胆的先锋实验，由十一位音乐家组成扩展编制，包括两位小号手、四位萨克斯手、双贝斯及鼓手。整首作品时长近四十分钟，在密集的集体即兴与个人长篇独奏之间交替展开，声响密集而充满张力。同年录制了两版完整演奏，黑胶首次将两个版本合并发行，呈现了同一构思下不同的即兴走向。制作人Bob Thiele主导了这一对自由爵士运动具有宣言意义的录音。此版本由Verve Vault再版发行，将这一现代爵士史上的里程碑作品以完整面貌重新呈现给听众。

items.body:
Ricardo Villalobos runs rings around two trax from goat (JP)’s 2025 dance score in three durational, tempo-sloped parts for Paris-based Latency. Japanese no wave asceticism meets haughty house trot and lizard-hipped slink - 35 mins of it!

In their own ways, both Ricky V and Goat (JP) are no strangers to the weirder ends of the ‘floor, each excelling at threading the most sinuous grooves to the most fanciful purposes. Now brought together by Parisian electronic atelier Latency, Villalobos pursues his preceding reworks of Reza Mortazevi’s hand-played percussion with a supple loosening of goat (jp)’s crystalline pulses in three distinct variations, tweaking the original timbales of ‘Orin’ away from avant-dance roots into 9 mins of heavily infectious wiggle swarmed with class, over-the-shoulder vocals, kinda something from his ‘Sei Es Drum’ series. ‘Factory’ on the other hand is taken for a longer ride in contrasting parts, recalibrating its cogs with a grittier swivel and unravelled loops of the OG in Variation 1, then slowing it all to a superb 110BPM version bound for the *special* folder and loosey goosey ends of the day/night.

items.body:
Seattle-based electronica artist Hünter makes a strong first impression with their debut volley of intricately amorphous rhythms and probing tones, in arrangements blending club, neo-classical, and sound designer urges, FFO Svbkvlt, Æ, Björk

“Of Paradise welcomes Seattle-based artist Hünter with his sophomore album, Mica, a sublime addition to the label’s ever-evolving musical catalogue and one that quickly acquires almost mythical status.

Focused on the relationship between the digital age and the environment, Mica explores the extraction of natural resources, identity, memory, and what remains. A fusion of ambient soundscapes and deconstructed club rhythms, Mica questions erosion as both a physical and cultural consequence of modern consumption, encouraging listeners to reevaluate their relationship with nature, technology, and excess.

Available as a limited edition 12” and digital album, Mica responds to overstimulation; music that breathes slowly, punctuated by occasional moments of tension, provides periods of stillness and reflection interrupted by the intensity of digital life and environmental anxiety. This album isn’t merely a collection of songs; it’s an atmosphere to inhabit.”

items.body:
Patrick Gräser, AKA Answer Code Request, was one of the defining producers of Berghain's second generation.  First emerging  in the early '10s, Gräser was producing industrial-strength techno influenced by the hardcore continuum, serving Berlin techno with a twist of UK rave and '90s IDM. 

As a resident of the Berlin club, he was an heir apparent to mentor Marcel Dettmann—only instead of Dettmann's penchant for EBM and new wave, it sounded like Gräser had spent formative years clubbing on Fridays during the Sub:stance heydays. The pair of records he released during that period—2014's    Code   and 2018's   Gens  —remain high watermarks of the Ostgut Ton catalogue. 

New LP  Halo  picks up where  Gens  left off. The synth work alternates between chillout tent comedown and Japanese-school psychedelia, where the melodies seem to twist and turn in on themselves. The sweeping chords on "Shine Deep" are borderline too celestial, but just when we're about to drift off into the ether, Gräser spices up the break with a kick drum that sounds lifted out of a Shed record. 

The title track, on the other hand, hews closer to something DJ Nobu might play. "Halo" starts with what sounds like an army of buzzing cybernetic mosquitos trapped in a closet seeking out blood, before unleashing a closed hi-hat and freewheeling bassline halfway through. It transforms the track into a proper barnstormer, as well as being a callback to an era-specific Berlin techno sound. 

Gräser remains able to infuse a wide range of emotional depth into the austere templates of techno. There's plenty of that across  Halo  (see also the Autechre synth squiggles and syncopated groove on "Bliphar"). But he also pushes himself out of his comfort zone: "D-Fracture" is like listening to a techno remake of Ed Rush and Optical's dark drum & bass classic,  Wormhole , as the creeping feedback consumes the stereo field like a horror movie garbage disposal. 

The opener, "Fading Shadows", also lets Gräser write the  Selected Ambient Works  song he's always wanted (in fact, the track might be even better without the kick drum that eventually does come in). These aren't necessarily new tricks, but a sign that Gräser isn't resting on his laurels just yet. 

Times have changed since Gräser first released music, when Berghain and Ostgut Ton represented a sonic vanguard. The club is no longer the musical weathervane it once was, even as it remains a cultural flashpoint.  But it's also true that the Berghain sound was never monolithic. 

Nostalgia might have us all imagine it was cold, steely minimalism from Saturday to Monday afternoon, but things were always weirder. Hell, just listen to Dettmann's jump cut to Kevin Saunderson's "Just Want Another Chance" on   Berghain 002  , or go to a recent REEF party for that matter.  Gräser, in this sense, embodies the club's more wide-ranging ethos. While  Halo  may not represent the future of techno, it still showcases one of the best producers of the past 20 years.

items._cn_summary: Answer Code Request 的新专辑延续了其以柏林俱乐部为根基的工业强度电子声响，同时大幅拓展声音边界。专辑在冷峻的 techno 框架中融入九十年代 IDM、日本学派迷幻合成器氛围与 Autechre 式声波扭曲，旋律呈现自我折叠的旋绕感。不同曲目策略各异：开篇近似 Aphex Twin 式环境作品，标题曲以密闭式嗡嗡音效切入后转向浩室底鼓驱动的燃点段落，D-Fracture 则将丛林鼓线与恐怖片式反馈吞噬感合为一体。制作人在严格的 techno 范式内注入丰富的情感深度与异质元素，未落入模式化窠臼，但评论亦指出整张作品并非面向未来的彻底革新，而是对既有技艺的精炼延续。

items.body: Let it happen at our peril. This is the title of the final track on We Vote Force Majeure , a powerfully free set of collective improvisations by the band Hyper Elastic Jinx, and it is a prophetic warning. For instance, climate change is projected to increase coastal flooding around Norway, Denmark, and Germany, where the musicians on this album primarily reside, by a factor of 10, 100, or even 1000 depending upon emissions scenarios. “Let It Happen At Our Peril,” the song, opens with two saxophones, one the alto of Signe Emmeluth, one a tenor played by Nana Pi, both of whom are deeply connected to the Scandinavian experimental music scene. The saxophones warp and twist around each other as the song progresses. By mid-tune, the piece has erupted into a catastrophic explosion of sound, with drummer Halym Kim crashing down on the snare and cymbals, and guitarist Keisuki Matsuno firing hits and chords full of color and fuzzy, chorus-filled reverb that sounds to me like it's played on an old Fender amp built in the 1970s. Kim and Nana Pi have played extensively together on the Northern European scene, including on the 2022 album Tactical Maybe , a gorgeous and raucous experimental work I highly encourage everyone to check-out. Matsuno, on the other hand, has ties to the John Zorn world, playing on Zorn’s Bagatelles Volume 11 in 2022 with Jim Black. Emmeluth, of course, has forged a fiery reputation as dynamo of what the Free Jazz Collective has called The New Danish Thing . But We Vote Force Majeure is not about its individual performers. It is an album of collective free improvisation for which all musicians share equally in the song-writing credits. It is a community in communion with the greater good, and despite my use of the word catastrophic in the previous paragraph, notes about the album on the Barefoot Records webpage state “The album is not an invocation of catastrophe, but a longing for a superior and irresistible force that people can’t ignore - a force that focuses on social values, cultural exchange and ecological sustainability.” Despite this persistent optimism of the will, the album is meant to remind listeners “that the world and the structures we are living in are not socially, economically, ecologically or politically sustainable and benefit only a minority of people.” The album warns it is “Always the Others,” the title of the second work on the record. Experts on the history of concentration camps point out that camps functioning in far away times and places are easily labeled as evil, while those erected and running here and now are commonly believed to hold the real bad guys. The individuals held in these places are so quickly othered. And, it is so easy for fascism to take root when its citizens believe it is always the others who face genuine danger. Here in the United States, for instance, by April 2026, 42,000 people with no prior criminal records were being detained in camps throughout the United States. These are camps for the mass detention of civilians, not war-time prisoners, who have not been given due process and were detained on the prejudicial basis of a larger group identity. Perhaps “Let It Happen At Our Peril” and “Always the Others” call back and ahead philosophically to the album’s fourth track “Zero Point 75.” In the world of optometry, +0.75 Diopters is the lowest level used in a prescription to correct short-sightedness. The short sightedness of humanity may be a reality, but it is still at a correctable state. I don’t think the musicians play programmatically on this album, but I find it fitting that Halym Kim opens this song playing the drums as though it were the ticking of a manual alarm clock. We can only remain short sighted for so much time. So, instead of shrinking away in despair of catastrophe, we can choose now to function like the example set by the musicians on this record: individually contributing to a working group dynamic. Here, this musical dynamic is one where the energy rises and washes over the listener more than any individual solo. The value is located in the spontaneous and present collective, not in a perfected show of musical virtuosity. It is force majeure : a force of such superior power that it is irresistible. And, as displayed on this wonderfully powerful album, it can be used as a force for good. We Vote Force Majeure by Hyper Elastic Jinx Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由北欧实验即兴乐团 Hyper Elastic Jinx 创作，是一张集体自由即兴作品，创作署名由全体成员平等共享。乐评以专辑终曲为切入点，将其标题解读为对气候危机与极权风险的预警。音乐层面，乐评重点分析了终曲开篇两支萨克斯的缠绕与变形、中段鼓与吉他引发的爆裂声响，以及吉他手 Matsuno 与 John Zorn 圈子及 Bagatelles 系列的关联；萨克斯手 Emmeluth 则被定位为'新丹麦之声'的代表人物。乐评进一步将专辑的政治意涵引向'他者化'主题，结合美国拘押营现状展开讨论，并引用厂牌页面所述：专辑并非召唤灾难，而是呼唤一种不可忽视、聚焦社会价值与生态可持续性的力量。整体而言，乐评将音乐文本与社会批判紧密结合，对即兴细节与政治语境均有较深入剖析。

items.body: Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release, Under an Endless Sky . In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari, Songs of Compassion is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics. Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari | Photo by Maria Assunta Karini Songs of Compassion has two challenges for the listener. The first is the music, called variously avant-garde, ambient, modal, non-linear, and a few more. It is played mostly on pianos mixed in and out of the foreground, sometimes doubled, and sometimes out of phase, joined by strings, woodwinds, synth washes, and steely sounds. Initially disorienting, the music serves to remind us how locked our minds are to Western notions of harmonic movement. It speaks of alternative musical narratives much older and much further away. They are songs that subvert the song: more like Steve Reich than Steve Stills; more like Phillip Glass than Phil Collins. UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY - Pale Wanderer At the same time, there are the poetic yet strikingly contemporary lyrics. �Pale Wanderer� talks about the fact that authoritarianism needs willing accomplices, describing what happens �When you make a deal with darkness.� UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY (Dorothy Moskowitz, Francesco Paolo Paladino e Luka Chino Ferrari) by Silentes �Charlottesville� (written with the late Joe Byrd) evokes the time not long ago when torch-wielding nazis, proud of the metaphoric Ns on their tunics, chanted the antisemitic tropes paraphrased in Moskowitz�s words, �We�ll be one people, pure of race/No greedy throng could take our place� . Besides the overtly political lyrics, in the tradition of 1960s protest songs, there are also thoughtful meditations on mortality and our place in the universe. The message is high-minded yet sincere and direct. World weary and wise, Moskowitz�s voice inhabits the evocative philosophical lyrics with the authority of a skilled method actor. The melodies unfold like streams of consciousness, rising and falling, not following expected diatonic chord progressions, but honouring, instead, the value of each word. Moskowitz�s piano acts as another voice and sometimes a kind of Greek chorus commenting on the proceedings. The surrounding music frames, creates pulses and dissonances, and shimmers. The return of Dorothy Moskowitz with her renamed project has arrived in a moment quite similar to the times that spawned its predecessor. Political division, unrest, and uncertainty always generate artistic reaction, and United States of Alchemy roared back to life with their epic 24-minute opening track �Under an Endless Sky� in 2023, serving perhaps as an �In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida� for our times. Songs of Compassion continues to challenge how we think about our world. It�s music that defies the song form, while doing exactly what music is supposed to do�enrich the human condition. Find the artist online. The title track from the 2023 U.S. of Alchemy recording Under an Endless Sky by Dorothy Moskowitz & United States of Alchemy Further reading Cris Derksen - The Visit (Review) Tiny Sun - Vanishment (Review) Maria Ka - Di Mashin (Review) Further listening You will find a number of Dorothy Moskowitz's works on Race The Sky , most recently on Podgrammes #022 and #019.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Dorothy Moskowitz与两位意大利合作者Francesco Paolo Paladino和Luca Chino Ferrari共同完成，收录十一首歌曲。音乐以钢琴为核心，叠加弦乐、木管、合成器泛音与金属质感音色，采用非线性和调式化手法，刻意打破西方和声运动的惯性听觉习惯，呈现类似Steve Reich和Philip Glass的简约重复美学。歌词兼具诗意与政治性，从《Pale Wanderer》对威权主义合谋者的揭示，到与已故Joe Byrd合作的《Charlottesville》直面新纳粹集会现场，延续1960年代抗议歌曲传统。Moskowitz的人声演绎带有阅历沉淀的权威感，旋律如同意识流般起伏，不依附传统功能和声，而是让每个词获得独立的重量。专辑诞生于一个与前辈乐队时代相似的政治分裂时刻，将音乐实验与社会批判编织为统一的艺术声明。

items.body: Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka I n the High Middle Ages, Hildegard of Bingen said that �The truly holy person welcomes all that is earthly.� William Blake declared in The Marriage of Heaven and Hell (1790) that �Exuberance is beauty.� In 1855, Walt Whitman published the poem �Song Of Myself, 51� in Leaves of Grass , which contains the famous line �I am large, I contain multitudes.� I�m just skimming the surface of mystical experience, of those struck by wonder and an all-encompassing insight into how people fit into the �grand scheme of things.� At some point on this trajectory, the boundary between the religious and the secular breaks down and simply being human becomes the ultimate wow. Which brings us to Polish artist Maria Ka�s latest album Di Mashin . Ka found that her family had Jewish roots, a discovery that led her to an immersion in Jewish studies and the Yiddish language. As on 2023�s Der Hemshekh , she unreels original songs written in Yiddish, embracing a politically active feminism and a committed meta-universality. Her musical vision is fragrantly mystical, and she presents us with a whole Yiddish cosmos. While not sharing the same type of musical style, Ka reminds me of John Zorn�s aesthetic of mixing the grotesque and the sacred into Jewish experimental music. She also reminds me of the woman on the phone sampled on Wally Brill�s Jewish cantorial electronica album The Covenant (2007), who confesses she can�t sleep after hearing someone in a bar talking about the Book of Ezekiel and being haunted by the vision of Jews arriving from a future space-time. She sees that we are all suspended in webs of relationships. She is also deeply aware of how we are subject to larger social forces and structures � which sometimes must be met with radical action -- that are the machinery of life. There is a heavy dose of electro and punkish attitude spinning through her musical universe. Ostensibly, the album is divided between electronic and rock tracks, but there is a consistency to the sound that is united in loopy joy. At its best, Di Mashin is sly and sexy. Opening track �Alef � Tsentauri Disko� finds Ka in the city, musing on the seaside, wriggling like a snake at night, and watching Gdańsk wake up. �I often Dream about Cosmos, about the Land above the Earth / overhead / Alef Centauri Jewish disco!� she sings, set to a thumping urban electro grind. (See video below) Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka �Vos iz dos?� is a standout, more in the �rock� vein, with Ka howling a debate over the Yiddish language itself. Perhaps it is based in a critique that she received, as she starts with What is this? Maria, what is this? I constantly hear it, it has not finished You speak no Yiddish!/ It�s so easy! Your language is incorrect, mistaken is your speech and dialect! � Given that Ka is producing new modern songs in Yiddish, there is something disarming in acknowledging the tension over who might claim ownership of language itself. Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka �SuperNove� might remind listeners of Jacob wrestling with God, if that battle was done to an �80s new wave beat. Ka has visions of the past, the Old World and old demons, and she fights a ghost that rises to block her way: � I fought him with Strength, punched him with my both hands�I triumphed over him! I myself � I did triumph over him! � And after that victory, � it�s a great Surprise � the Past melted in the Cosmic Blast! � Ka also seems to be challenging herself, pointing in new directions. �Di Kosmish motorn (Cosmic engines)� brought to mind the former Warsaw Village Band�s blues-influenced singer Maja Kleszcz. Depeche Mode�s (fronted by Dave Gahan, of Jewish ancestry) forays into fusing electronica with blues might be another touchpoint. Hearing the cosmic engines like a modern day Pythagoras, she is awestruck by hearing the cosmic engines in her head. �Dos geverk (The mechanism)� offers some grinding guitars to convey the constant motion of the daily rat race � echoed later on by the title track, �Di Mashin (The Machine),� which peels back the layers of society to reveal the incessant obsession for money. The music of �The Machine� is hyperspeed cabaret, close to madness. The system demands more money � but she indicates that she is a spanner in the works, working to bring it down: � I watch the machine�s death / Full and steadily red is my hand in the end. � Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka Feminist politics come to the fore on �Ikh bin a froy (I am a woman),� and Ka reminds me a bit of the divine Ms. H of Bingen chanting over a motoric beat. She refuses to be hemmed in by structures, signaling that the Forest is her home, the stars her friends; �I wake up every day / and new scroll create.� Album closer �Di milkhome� (War)� is more future blues, transposing war, empty shipyards, and advice from her mother that all miseries will end and freedom will navigate the turmoil �like huge ships at Sea.� Di Mashin is possessed by such a singular offbeat vision and personal mythology that I wonder where Maria Ka will take her Yiddishfuturism next�Perhaps beyond our solar system, grooving on an interstellar plane with her band wriggling like snakes. Find the artist online. Further listening: Maria Ka - Der Hemshekh Warsaw Village Band & Bassałyki - Sploty WoWaKin - Kraj za miastem

items._cn_summary: 波兰艺术家Maria Ka在发现自身犹太血统后，以意第绪语创作原创歌曲，构建出一个融合电子律动与朋克态度的意第绪音乐宇宙。专辑横跨电子与摇滚两种风格，但贯穿始终的是循环往复的欢愉感。开场曲将城市夜晚的躁动与宇宙意象并置，电子节拍粗粝有力；另一首以摇滚骨架支撑，Ka以嚎叫般的唱腔回应外界对其意第绪语使用准确性的质疑，语言本身的政治性成为创作核心。乐评将Ka的美学与John Zorn的犹太实验音乐传统相提并论，强调她将神圣与怪诞、神秘主义与激进行动主义熔于一炉的独特视角，用母语创作本身就是对文化消逝的抵抗。

items.body: The Visit by cris derksen The Visit isn�t an album built on compromises. The fourth release from Derksen, a Canadian from the North TallCree Reserve on her father�s side, and with a Mennonite lineage from her mother, pushes and cajoles her visions, where it�s the opening, full-throated improvisation of �White Gladis 1� (with singer Jennifer Kreisberg) or the encompassing haunting mood that grows up around �Lyre Birds.� She�s primarily a cellist, one who works across genres; one of the great joys here is it�s impossible to attach any kind of handle to the music. Just as you think you have it nailed down, the next track is something different, as with the the cello and programming of �aabaakwad� which becomes the wordless singing of �New Heya.� The Visit by cris derksen There�s a raw, unfettered beauty to the album, music made with passion and no restraints. There are a couple of songs here, but nothing that conforms to expectations, altering gears and direction, as when the strings and brass that arrive from nowhere to take over �Buffalo Girls.� The Visit by cris derksen But the emotional centrepiece here is �Lyre Birds,� with Derksen�s cello weaving sparely around the shards of spoken words, leading into the fluttering piano arpeggios of �Nice And Clean.� This is an album of surprises, leading down strange lanes and around brilliant corners that offer startling new views. As both composer and musician, Cris Derksen is more than a singular talent; she�s a person with a vision for her music, and she keeps true to it here. The Visit is not an easy listen, but it is eminently satisfying. Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以大提琴为核心，跨越多个音乐领域，融合原住民传统与古典训练背景，展现出拒绝妥协的艺术姿态。作品结构开放多变，从全开即兴的《White Gladis 1》到氛围浓郁的《Lyre Birds》，每首曲目都走向不同方向：大提琴与电子编程交织的《aabaakwad》、以人声取代乐器的《新Heya》，以及突然转向的《Buffalo Girls》中弦乐与铜管的介入。整张专辑情绪饱满，以《Lyre Birds》为核心——大提琴稀疏地环绕着破碎的话语——随后过渡到钢琴琶音的《Nice And Clean》。专辑带领听众进入陌生的路径与意想不到的转角，作为作曲家和演奏者，Derksen展现出清晰的个人愿景，乐器与编程、传统与现代、自发与结构之间的对话贯穿始终。

items.body:
The jittery pulses and waking dream-like atmospheres of Dx2ov land on London’s Blank Mind for an album strafing between cut-up sound poetry and whisked garage-house.

“Dx2ov arrives on Blank Mind with Tonegues, his second vinyl LP following on from Interzona on Gost Zvuk in 2024. The LP title is a wordplay on the idea of speaking in tongues and sonic tonalities, echoing the process and dialogue that went into creating the record. Taken from a vast archive of material from 2019-2025, these ideas were arranged with the collaboration of label owner Sam Purcell and then completed with the long-distance assistance of Toupaz.

Tonegues is best seen through the lens of a beat-tape, with the playful flow and variety that the format provides, bursting with oddball ideas and punctuated with intangible vocal samples. Much like the LP’s beguiling, hand-drawn artwork by Wolfgang Matuschek, it is a glimpse into an inner world, a portal to somewhere uncanny and strange borne through imagination.

Light dub flourishes mix with footwork/IDM hybrids and understated, melancholic synthesis on ‘2018’, whilst the loose, rhythmic march of ‘Fon32’ evokes the dusty beatdown styles of early 2000s Detroit downtempo records. Whilst on one of the LP highlights ‘Trout’ he lays down a gleefully strange bed for the surrealist storytelling of Jacob Dwyer about interactions with dogs, dripping old houses and a perennial wish for the phone to ring with a heavy dub poetry slant. Dx2ov swiftly moves through more footwork adjacent, almost bedroom hyper-pop territories with a penchant for gabber kicks on ‘No Strings (feat DJ Paprika)’ and the maximalism of album closer 'Demetch' which continues in the tradition of wonky, mid-2010s UK bass music flips. The outcome is a confounding, unorthodox piece of work, zigzagging between forms, textures and moods.”

items._cn_summary: 这是一张在伦敦地下厂牌 Blank Mind 发行的实验电子专辑，标题取自"说方言"的谐音，暗示声音与语言的对话关系。创作者从2019至2025年间积累的大量素材中精选编排，与厂牌主理人Sam Purcell合作，并经远程协助完成混音。整张作品以节拍合辑的逻辑组织，充满碎片化的声音设计与若隐若现的人声采样。曲目在轻盈的dub质感、IDM与footwork混合体、卧室hyper-pop、gabber kick等元素间频繁跳转，客席说唱以dub poetry风格讲述关于狗、老房子与等待电话的荒诞叙事。专辑视觉采用手绘风格，与音乐共同构建出一个陌生而内向的内心世界，呈现形式与情绪的高度统一。

items.body:
Puristic electro-techno hydrolicks heavily inspired by classic James Stinson & Gerald Donald, dispatched by the sound’s Dutch torch carriers.

An album-length project spread over 2 x 12”s, ‘Vaporwave I’ trades in classiest brand of Drexciyan worship. The title and loose, livewire flex of ‘Gyrodyne’ hints at Drexicya’s influence via their affiliates, Ultradyne, whilst the vocoders and propulsive 4/4 pulse of ‘Component Zero’ nods in Aux 88’s direction, next to a standout lightshow of harmonised arps on a sleazy bassline in ‘Handjob’. The sturdy linearity of ‘Trust Machine’ check for early EBM and coldwave influence on classic ‘90s electro, and ‘Avec de L’esprit’ harnesses pure 313-via-Harbour City horsepower.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张向底特律经典电声传统致敬的专辑，项目以双十二寸黑胶形式发行，完整呈现了 Drexciya 式的冷峻美学。制作团队为荷兰的电子声音传承者，整张专辑以纯正的电子脉冲为骨架，融合早期 EBM 与冷潮的线性结构。开篇曲目从旋翼直升机的意象切入，暗示 Ultradyne 流派的影响；中段引入声码器与四四拍推进节拍，并向 Aux 88 的方向靠拢；另有曲目在谐波琶音与低频贝斯线之间构建出流畅的律动。专辑整体克制而精密，音色选择具有工业质感，节奏设计强调机械性与功能性之间的平衡，对于熟悉底特律电声谱系的听众而言，是一次扎实且忠诚的回溯。

items.body:
Serious techno traction from Surgeon on his sleekly powerful first album in five years, sounding like the Brummie dynamo has properly got to grips with the modular array he’s built over the past decade.

A true hallmark of great electronic music producers is the ability to sound like yourself no matter the kit. On ‘Crash Recoil’ Surgeon stamps his signature on every tune via a crisply refined touch on his modular set-up, wresting eight tracks of chewy, roiling momentum with a militant discipline and crafty turns of phrase. Surgeon albums have long been the place to go for his more experimental works, especially the likes of ‘Basictonalvocabulary’ (1997) and ‘Breaking The Frame’ (2011), and this new one finds him balancing urges toward freakier, brutally sensual sound design and the steeliest yet supple club rhythms in a subtle upgrade and redefinition of his sound that still bears traces of the lithe, hands-on tekkerz that have driven his work since the mid ‘90s.

The trax are held in taut flux between electro and techno, proper, vacillating on/off the beat in restlessly rolling forms. ‘Oak Bank’ spends the first half plumbing deepwater electro, resolving to tunnelling techno pulse midway and building a heady velocity. The rest of thallium swillers around this style, from entrancing hydrodynamics on ‘Second Magnitude Stars’ to the outstanding grind of ‘Metal Pig’, and the sinuous, dark sidewinder ‘Leadership Contest’, with hypnotic effect on ‘Masks & Archetypes’ giving way tot he trance-techno of ‘Subcultures’ in a flow not dissimilar to a DJ or live set.
items._genre: techno / electro / experimental electronic / modular synth
items._cn_summary: Surgeon暌违五年推出的专辑以模块化合成器为核心，呈现八首兼具实验性与俱乐部节奏的作品。整张专辑在techno与electro之间游走，结构充满张力：部分曲目先潜入深水般的electro段落，再转向隧道式techno脉冲，速度层层递进。制作上强调'嚼劲十足'的律动与军事化纪律感的张力平衡，声音设计偏向粗粝而感官化的方向，同时保留了自九十年代中期以来的灵动手工质感。从催眠质感的氛围段落到迷幻trance-techno，曲目排列模拟DJ或现场set的流动逻辑。对偏好实验电子与暗潮工业交汇区域的听众而言，这张专辑在类型框架内实现了较为扎实的声音重新定义。

items.body:
A real bona fide alltimer, Jeff’s legendary ’95 live template for high-velocity, hypnotic DJing still kills like little else 30 years later.​

Shelling 38 tracks in 67 minutes, broken in three parts by daring fade outs at peak time, Mills delivers a masterful example of techno coming into its own in the mid ‘90s as a unique facet of the era’s intense feedback loop between dancers, DJ and technology. In all acknowledgement that we’re probably preaching to the choir here, the Detroit dynamo comes absolutely ruthless with it, deploying all the tricks learned from his days as a notoriously skilled hip hop and electro DJ, to a more linear format that best allows for optimal momentum and on/off-the beat EQ tweaking and cross-fader chops.

In a 2020s of instant CDJ gratification, where posers spend more time exhibiting armpits and pouting than locked-in, there’s an extra frisson of thrill to knowing Mills did this analog, riding the pitch adjuster, stroking the platter, and even turning the power off, which all lends an extra, un-quantised tension and funk to the process that can’t be replicated by digitally-locked DJ formats. They both have their place, but this mix is basically the dogs bollocks and never to be repeated. We envy you if it’s your first go.
items._genre: techno / hypnotic techno / electronic DJ mix
items._cn_summary: 这张1995年的现场DJ混音专辑展现了一位底特律电子音乐先驱的高超技艺：在67分钟内串联38首曲目，以三段式结构布局，在高潮处大胆淡出再切入，形成持续的动能与张力。混音手法延续了其早年嘻哈与电子时期的搓碟与均衡器技巧，移植到更线性的techno框架中，强调即兴与节奏操控。评论特别强调了这是一场纯模拟设备的现场——手动调节pitch、抚触唱片、甚至直接关闭电源——这些无法被数字系统复制的操作赋予了音乐一种独特的未量化张力与律动。在CDJ时代即时满足的背景下，这种模拟现场的控制力与身体性显得尤为珍贵，被视为90年代中期techno作为一种独立音乐形态走向成熟的标志范例。

items.body:
Ezekiel Honig's glitchy, concréte house breakout, that originally surfaced nearly two decades ago, finally gets a new lease of life (and a fresh mastering job) thanks to the Keplar imprint.

Back in 2008, the world was already over microhouse. The glitchy, short-lived micro-genre had burned bright for a short moment; Philip Sherburne had coined the term in 2001 and by the time Akufen's 'My Way' had emerged just a year later it felt as if the shine had gone. Honig's 'Surfaces of a Broken Marching Band' arrived in 2008 and sounded like reformed traces of the recent past. The backbone was 4/4, crawling towards a slinky 120BPM minimal house, but the emotional content was completely different. This wasn't material that was aimed at the club or even the afterparty, it was loose, faded gear that Honig had made from meticulously collected foley sounds and environmental recordings - domestic elements that Matthew Herbert would be proud of.

And because the music slipped quietly into its own nook, it still sounds unique now, a record that deserves to be filed alongside Farben's early 12"s and Kit Clayton's iconic 'Nek Sanalet', even Ricardo Villalobos's primo gear - just peep the title track and tell us it doesn't sound like 'Easy Lee' made with a broken shortwave radio and a pinball table. Needless to say, if you're into Mark Templeton (who incidentally appears twice on this record) or the soon-to-be-hauntological Y2K aesthetic, you'll need to grab it without delay.
items._cn_summary: 这张2008年的专辑经过Keplar厂牌重新母带处理后重见天日。Ezekiel Honig以4/4拍为骨架，节奏缓慢爬行至120BPM的极简浩室，但情感内核截然不同——他精心采集日常环境中的物件声响与田野录音，将其融入音乐纹理，创造出一种松散、褪色的听感，不为俱乐部而生，也不为派对而设。评论将这张作品与Farben早期单曲、Kit Clayton的经典以及Ricardo Villalobos的顶级制作相提并论，认为它至今仍保持着独特性。专辑中还出现了Mark Templerton的作品，暗示其与Y2K hauntology美学之间的关联。整体而言，这是一张从微浩室废墟中重建的声音档案，用foley采样和环境录音为冷感节拍注入体温。

items.body:
French musical outlaw Pascal Comelade presents a selection of eccentric covers recorded over the last four decades, including madcap versions of classics from Nirvana, The Kinks, Captain Beefheart, MC5, The Ramones and Bob Dylan.

Since the '70s, Comelade has been questioning the logic of so-called experimental music, using cheap instruments like singing saws, recorders and toy pianos to make covers of modern standards - rock songs, easy listening earworms - that flip expectations. If you've never come across his solo productions or his work with his legendary Bel Canto Orquestra, then 'Métaphysique Du Hit-Parade' is the ideal introduction - a selection of Comelade's finest covers with a couple of brand new ones (junkshop versions of Dylan's 'Girl from the North Country' and Nirvana's 'Come As You Are') thrown in for good measure. 

Now none of this should work on any metric, but there's an earnestness to Comelade's music that makes it hit surprisingly hard. Just check the hideously detuned bontempi version of 'Sunny Afternoon' and try not to crack a smile, or his ramshackle take on 'Purple Haze'. It ain't pretty, but it works.
items._genre: experimental / outsider music / toy instruments / avant-pop / lo-fi covers
items._cn_summary: 法国音乐人Pascal Comelade自七十年代以来始终在质疑所谓实验音乐的逻辑，他以廉价乐器——锯琴、竖笛、玩具钢琴——重新解构摇滚经典，将Nirvana、The Kinks、Captain Beefheart、MC5、The Ramones、Bob Dylan等作品拆解为怪异的低保真翻唱。这张合辑收录了他四十年来最出色的翻唱作品，并加入了两首全新录制，包括对Dylan《Girl from the North Country》和Nirvana《Come As You Are》的废品店风格改编。Comelade的音乐拒绝精致，走调、粗糙、破旧，但其中蕴含的诚恳态度使作品具备了出人意料的感染力。那些用破旧电子琴演绎的走调版本既不好听也不漂亮，却自有一种独属于解构主义的趣味。对偏好实验与前卫美学的听众而言，这是接触这位法国异端音乐人作品的理想切入点。

items.body:
A sequel to 2024's rock history redux 'This is BASIC', the spartan 'BASIC' boasts a new lineup, featuring Tortoise's Doug McCombs, and introduces Tuareg and Highlife rhythms while retaining the electroacoustic bent of their debut.

'This is BASIC' was a great idea handled very well; the project was initiated by Chris Forsyth and Nick Millevoi as a reaction to Robert Quine and Fred Maher's 'Basic', a hypnotic mid-'80s cult classic that welded nascent drum machine loops to post-punk guitar phrases. The two players wondered if there was a way that thread might be followed a few decades later and invited Mikel Patric Avery to help out with the electronics. Since then, Millevoi has dropped out but he's been replaced by McCombs, who initially crewed up to help the band tour their debut and ended up sticking around for recording afterwards.

As you might expect, 'BASIC' skews a little more post-rock than its predecessor, with McCombs' signature playing front and center, at least at first, but the band do their best to keep folding in fresh influences, charting a course where guitar music wasn't constantly being deconstructed and reinvented to harmonize with cultural waves. Forsythe's usage of Tuareg riffs is particularly effective (check 'Loose Cannon') and puts a completely different spin on McCombs' basslines and 'Index of Memories' is fascinating, a whirring mass of xenharmonic synth flutes, skipping beats and druggy guitar lines that sounds like it's about to be pounced on by Pete Swanson and Jed Bindeman's Freedom To Spend imprint.
items._genre: post-rock / experimental rock / electroacoustic / Tuareg fusion
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是2024年《This is BASIC》的续作，原班人马中Nick Millevoi退出后，由Tortoise乐队的Doug McCombs接任贝斯手，Chris Forsyth与Mikel Patrick Avery继续合作。项目起源于对Robert Quine与Fred Maher八十年代中期的cult经典《Basic》的再回应——将鼓机循环与后朋克吉他短语焊接在一起。本作在保持电声实验倾向的基础上，引入了Tuareg与Highlife节奏元素，呈现出比前作更偏后摇滚的气质。McCombs标志性的贝斯演奏贯穿始终，Forsyth对Tuareg riff的运用别具一格，为贝斯线注入了全新色彩。《Index of Memories》尤其值得关注，xenharmonic合成器笛声、跳跃节拍与迷幻吉他线条交织成复杂的声响网络，散发着迷幻实验的气息。整体而言，这是一次跨文化节奏与电声美学的有机融合。

items.body:
MEGO mainstay Tujiko Noriko returns to the label for her sixth venture, a double-album celebration of her cat Pon that's brimming with eccentricity and positivity. It's pop music on some level, but anchored by cinematic whimsy and the unique production touches that have had us following her every move for the last quarter century. RIYL Björk, Tenniscoats, Astrid Sonne, Julia Holter, Ichiko Aoba.

Films have always had an influence on Noriko's music; in 2005, she even embarked on a film career in earnest, working on various experimental films until her proper feature 'Kuro' had matured to completion in 2017. So it's hardly surprising that her experience with film soundtracks - she handled the score for 2020's 'Surge' and 2024's 'He's Watching You' - has impacted her solo work. Her last album, the sublime 2LP elegy 'Crépuscule I & II' was an attempt by Noriko to collide her two creative worlds, meditating on nocturnal themes that seemed to hum with widescreen energy. And this latest record picks up where it left off, looking back over her relationship with her cat Pon who recently died in an accident. 'Pon' is a poppier record than its predecessor and doesn't dwell on sadness; its cinematic cues are hopeful, light and affecting, sculpted expertly by Noriko to give weight to her inner voice, the naive, intimate utterances that have characterized her music since the very beginning.

At first, it's not clear where we're headed. 'Only on Love', the album's skittering opening track, galvanizes Noriko's classic sound, letting her half-whispered vocals soar across pitchy drones and slow, metallic glitches. Noriko introduces us to the pop side of her personality first, with cool-headed, languid wordless hooks (check the gorgeous 'Bosom') and tight cybernetic rhythms that split the difference between Matmos and Pan Sonic. But by the time we reach 'Kikoeru Pon' ("hearing Pon"), the tone has begun to shift; using environmental recordings and neoclassical flourishes inspired by Nicholes Britell's enduring 'If Beale Street Could Talk' cue 'Agape', Noriko brings hope into the mix, ushering us into her IRL space, where we can hear rain on the window and Pon purring. And it's this alchemical blend that makes 'Pon' so touching - using the emotional language she's learned from cinema, Noriko is able to spirit us away into Pon's world and her own, a fantasy space that's both tiny and theatrically immense.

On 'Knife of Yonder', that space is dreamlike and billowing, stretched out over 11 minutes of analog moans and evocative bursts of percussion, while on 'Beachside Cats', the album transforms into lighthearted tropical psychedelia, offering a palate cleanser before the dramatic high-point 'Bokuno Satellite', a fusion of wailing noirish theremins, sunny guitars, "easy listening" vibraphones and chipmunked vocal stutters. Like its predecessor, 'Pon' is a lengthy proposition, but Noriko keeps it moving by constantly morphing; like a film that assembles its various stylistic chunks into a devastating whole (we're looking at you, 'Resurrection'), the album benefits from repeat listens, where its set-pieces can be deconstructed with the knowledge of each devastating buildup and release. As Ebert and Siskel might have said: two thumbs up.
items._genre: experimental pop / electronic / cinematic / art pop
items._cn_summary: 日本实验电子音乐人Tujiko Noriko在MEGO厂牌发行的第六张专辑，以双碟篇幅纪念意外离世的宠物猫Pon。专辑延续她标志性的低语人声与电影化制作美学，将环境录音、新古典钢琴与赛博朋克节奏并置，呈现出从《Only on Love》的金属故障质感到《Beachside Cats》的热带迷幻的多样面貌。她将电影配乐经验融入个人创作，以Nicholes Britell式的希望弦乐与窗外雨声、猫的呼噜声交织，在私密记忆与广阔想象空间之间游走。整体比前作更具流行感，却不失怪癖与温度，是一位长期创作者对日常情感的精密声响化处理。

items.body:
Andrew Field-Pickering (aka Max D) and Matt Papich (aka Co La) consider the process of filmmaking on their fifth album, adding foley sounds, concrète, and snatched conversations to their loose-limbed melange of Jazz, post rock and dub soundscapes, featuring additional players more eaze, Motion Graphics, Dustin Wong, Jeremy Hyman and more to complete the picture. Anyone on the line from Tortoise to Conjoint - we urge you to check in.

Lifted’s last album 'Trellis', arrived on Peak Oil following a run of deployments for PAN and Max D's own Future Times imprint and took stock of their run until that point, a surreal collage of studio recordings with input from a few trusted collaborators - all of whom also appear on 'Movie'. But this new set feels more like a line in the sand, a statement record that focuses the core duo's skills around a loose concept: cinema. Woven into a very TNT-esque post rock landscape, the duo weave overlapping dialog, room recordings and found sounds, referencing the kind of multi-track recording style that helped Robert Altman bring 'Nashville' to life, as well as Apichatpong Weerasethakul’s “slow cinema" style, focusing on seemingly insignificant sound details in the mix.

On ‘The Ice Chewers' Field-Pickering and Papich put more eaze to good use, backing up her bass guitar, pedal steel and acoustic guitar parts with an arsenal of FX and broken drums. Using tape stop effects to pitch the material as if putting their thumb on the master, the duo sound as if they're tinkering with the reel, burning it out just like Ingmar Bergman did in 'Persona' to remind you it was all celluloid. Musically, it's again a throwback to Tortoise's enduring 'TNT', letting it dissolve completely before hitting us with the noir-ish 'Paranoids'. Here, foley sounds overlap with indistinct dialog and environmental echoes that the duo loop and echo, painting an indistinct picture of a film that might be as eerie as 'The Conversation' or as eroticised as 'Klute'. 

On 'Repossessed' they shift into chillier territory and nattily avoid the churned Carpenterisms that have been rinsed to an almost laughable extent for the last few decades. Their VHS gore-inspired 'Melts Very Nasty' also avoids the obvious route, hinting at the general aura by using Mezey and Motion Graphics' submerged synths and Moore's bagpipes for added tension. They even hold back a genuine belter for the end credits: the soft rock-inspired 'Midnight Snack' - a 5 minute coda that could have been an after-hours Prince jam back in the day. Basically, even if you think you've got a lid on Lifted, 'Movie' really takes things to another level.
items._cn_summary: Lifted的第五张专辑《Movie》以电影制作为核心概念，Andrew Field-Pickering（Max D）与Matt Papich（Co La）将foley音效、具体音乐、截取的对话片段融入松散的后摇滚骨架中，融汇爵士、即兴和dub音景。专辑邀请了more eaze、Motion Graphics、Dustin Wong等多位乐手参与，风格参考了Tortoise的《TNT》、Robert Altman的多轨录音美学以及Apichatpong Weerasethakul的慢电影手法。曲目中模拟磁带停转效果、环境回响与潜没合成器交织，从chillier的《Repossessed》到软摇滚式的终曲《Midnight Snack》，在拼贴与氛围之间找到平衡，是一张概念统一、声音层次丰富的实验之作。

items.excerpt:
Autechre's classic debut album from 1993.

Autechre’s peerless debut album, Incunabula is reissued as a facsimile copy of the original, 1993 release, replete with silver-printed gatefold jacket.

We’re not going to bang on about this too much, but you should know by now that Incunabula is one of the cornerstones of modern electronic music, one of the pinnacles of the British rave epoch and among the most life-affirming records ever, bar none.

Aye, it’s 100% essential.

items.body:
Originally released in 2009, Capri is a concept album composed of fragmented vignettes, lost minutes and scenes from an idyllic imagining.

"A collection of brief moments, suspended shimmers, and frail settings, Capri was never meant to be more than its own thin veneer; a naked and subtle wash of saturated and semi-transparent colors, rolling as gently as ocean waves against rocky beaches, of fading afternoon sunlight, of momentary experience. Peaceful yet isolated, quiet yet collapsing, they are fading moments without definite borders, directions, or conclusion.

Remastered by Stephan Mathieu from the original tapes, and expanded to include the complete recordings excluded from the 2009 CD edition, this collection is finally present in its complete form in the deluxe edition. All music by Danielle Baquet and Will Long, 2007-2008."

items.body: A peaceful, singular, and cozy post-ambient journey made of lush sounds, with some chilling moments based on fragmented memories, that will ravish listeners of digitalized tape music and carefully crafted, slowly moving soundscapes. A vast array of minimal acoustic gestures I discovered the Brooklyn-based Build Buildings years ago with the superb release Ecotone on the recommended Laaps Records. Ben Tweel (alias Build Buildings) is a versatile and skilled sound researcher with an interest in deep ecology and in the essence of sound. His soundscapes are mostly instrumental, playing with a vast array of minimal acoustic gestures, effects, and objects, sonically morphed. I advise you to notably explore the music he released for Audiobulb. Molly Gochman is a prolific intermedia artist with an interest in the dialogue between abstract and musique concrète elements, often noticeable in her installations. This album approaches glitch-esque looped vignettes and micro-electronic sceneries, inviting the listener to delve into sentient and harmonious soundscapes filled with tiny elements, subtle variations, and dreamy resonances. The complete album is built on shimmering looped textures, fragmented yet allusive melodic lines obtained through manipulation of various string instruments, from harmonics to guitars. The pieces are also focused on the interaction between natural space and timbres, giving the ensemble a livelier and more organic dimension. The result flows dreamily, with meandering drone movements and micro-events that come together harmoniously in a slow-motion style. A peaceful, singular, and cozy post-ambient journey made of lush sounds, with some chilling moments based on fragmented memories, that will ravish listeners of digitalized tape music and carefully crafted, slowly moving soundscapes. Somewhere between Zane Trow, Chris Abraham, offthesky, and Andrew Tasselmyer. The album is delivered on beautiful vinyl accompanied by a digital version and comes highly recommended. Continuum is available on Unending Loop. [Bandcamp] Continuum by Build Buildings x Molly Gochman
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由布鲁克林声音研究者Ben Tweel（Build Buildings）与跨媒体艺术家Molly Gochman合作完成，以循环纹理和碎片化旋律线条为核心，通过对弦乐器（包括泛音与吉他）的采样与处理构建微电子声景。整体在缓慢流动的氛围中展开，融合了drone式的绵长音调、glitch式的循环片段以及musique concrète的具体声音素材，强调自然空间与音色之间的互动。作品中自然声学动作与电子变形手法并存，使声音在静态循环中持续生成微小变化，呈现出一种连贯而缓慢展开的听觉体验。评论将其归入post-ambient范畴，提及与Zane Trow、offthesky、Andrew Tasselmyer等声音艺术家的风格关联。专辑由独立厂牌Unending Loop发行，提供黑胶与数字版本，适合对缓慢展开的声景音乐感兴趣的听众。

items.body: B!CEP B.O.D.S. Knuckles on Stun Before discussing the new EP from Baltimore’s B!CEP, it’s probably worthwhile to address the obvious: they’re a lo-fi, punky EBM act whose songs are all about working out and getting swole, so yes, Diesel Dudes is the obvious point of comparison. That said, B.O.D.S. is still plenty enjoyable on those terms, with the duo (identified only as Long Head and Short Head, credited with MASS and ENDURANCE respectively) bringing appropriate sweat and strain. Gym anthem “Broken Face” opens things with percussion courtesy of crashing weights and rattly synths, slightly off-kilter but still coming across as properly yoked. Things pick up in terms of tempo on “Overthrow”, a speedy ode to overhead lifts, replete with various samples about muscle growth and a catchy shoutalong chorus. “Dead Weight” settles into a groove that actually recalls the thick rhythms of contemporary Portion Control, with snappy snares and another easy to chant basement show hook; “Why aren’t you stronger?/You’re gonna need to be stronger!” “Set to Fail” closes out the EP appropriately, zeroing in on a classic body music bassline that sets up its message of failure (of the progressive muscle variety in this case, but the metaphor works more broadly) as a step on the path to eventual victory. It’s the kind of thing that made their most obvious point of comparison so enjoyable, and damn if they don’t do a fine job of it themselves. B.O.D.S. by B!CEP Profligate Chewed Up self-released The last time we checked in with Profligate, the Ohio producer was veering away from the murky, beat-driven hybrid of EBM and darkwave which characterized their early releases with a more decidedly melodic and melancholy release in Too Numb To Know. Profligate’s first release in five years doesn’t just counteract that shift by moving back to six wholly rhythmically-driven pieces, but has yielded the most harsh and nasty music associated with the project by a long shot. Opener “Bin Men” introduces the grimy, hardware focused EP with circular, syncopating loops with little to no tonal focus whatsoever – it’s the sound of oil and grit-caked machinery falling in and out of step with itself. I can see some trying to draw a line between the clattering, constantly fracturing kicks of “Wrecked Exotic” and any number of modern dark techno producers, but really it feels like the skeleton of modern EBM stripped of any accoutrements and being dragged kicking and screaming back to the ur sources of first wave industrial. Closer “Burgled” is about as accessible as Chewed Up gets, and even that track has less in common with anything happening in Tresor than it does the misanthropic snarl of Autumns, one of the few current artists as gnarly and ornery as Profligate is here. items._cn_summary: 本篇乐评同时介绍了两张EP。B!CEP的《B.O.D.S.》以健身房为隐喻主题，是一首lo-fi朋克化的EBM作品，节奏急促有力，配以撞击器械的采样与粗粝合成器音色，歌词围绕举铁、肌肉增长与渐进负荷展开，情绪炽热粗粝。Profligate的《Chewed Up》则将EBM骨架剥离至最简，回溯至第一波工业音乐的粗砺根源，循环的同步硬件节拍缺乏调性中心，机械般咔嗒作响，更接近Autumns式愤世嫉俗的暗潮质感。两张作品虽主题一热一冷，但都深植于地下工业电子传统，独立发行，面向小众受众，未带明显跨界融合意图，但在各自的类型范畴内展现出明确的风格自觉与制作理念。

items.body: We’ll break the world Then build it new Remind them all With words we knew Blokkontroll’s debut, Odin Na Odin, comes from Kyiv with the blunt geometry of a bunker map and the physical impatience of a body already in motion. The solo project’s idea of each release as another Blok could have become tidy mythology, yet on this album, the concept feels practical, almost architectural: pressure placed upon pressure until a wall takes shape, until rhythm becomes shelter, weapon, and route. Its EBM is stripped to load-bearing parts. Drum machines advance with locomotive discipline, bass lines grind forward in locked angles, and synthesizers enter as machinery under strain, steel nerves pulled tight across empty rooms. The record has the air of a field recording taken during a blackout evacuation, where language has been bent by repetition and command, where the voice keeps returning because departure has become the only available grammar. Reverb and delay widen the room, then make that room feel less safe, turning every phrase into evidence from a system entering failure. Kult sharpens the album’s central impulse: leave, begin again, move before doubt can grow roots. The lyrics’ collective charge avoids simple uplift; its promise of breaking and rebuilding carries the severity of people who have learned that renewal may require damage. Across Odin Na Odin, that tension gives the vocals a peculiar authority. They sound like something that issued from someone close enough to fear to recognize it, close enough to action to spend no energy decorating it. Comparisons to Nitzer Ebb, Skinny Puppy, Front Line Assembly, and DAF make sense, though Blokkontroll’s language is narrower, drier, and more claustrophobic. The record gives repetition an abrasive force, using loops as walls against which the listener measures impact. Where many contemporary industrial records chase club release, Odin Na Odin keeps the floor under surveillance. Its movement is strict, the pleasure severe, the hooks buried in commands and metallic breath. Blokkontroll demonstrates that minimalism in this form feels enforced, severe, and functional. The tracks compact, compress, and seal, pulling every element towards a hard center. By the end, Odin Na Odin has mapped escape as a condition rather than a destination, turning personal rupture into a cold communal engine. It has weight, direction, and a frightening sense of use. For a debut, it feels alarmingly complete, a slab of industrial body music laid with care, anger, and exacting force in the dark. Listen to Odin Na Odin below and order the album here. items._cn_summary: 基辅单人项目Blokkontroll的首张专辑将EBM压缩至承重结构般的极简形态：鼓机以机车般的纪律推进，贝斯线以锐角刻进混音，合成器如受力金属般紧绷作响。评论将其置于Nitzer Ebb、Skinny Puppy、Front Line Assembly与DAF的影响谱系中，但强调其语汇更窄、更干、更具幽闭感。专辑以重复作为磨蚀性力量，把循环当作墙壁，听者在其上测量冲击。主题围绕离开、重建与行动展开，歌词拒绝简单的振奋，将破坏与更新绑在一起。整体呈现出一种纪律严明的运动感，地板始终处于被监视状态，钩子深埋于命令与金属气息之中。作为出道作，其完成度与功能性令人注目。

items.body: The men who honed my eyes and ears For the sight and for the sound He is not a friend of mine Budapest dream folk act Musica Moralia’s “Let’s Take Our Bones Out” is a haunting song that opens with a banjo carrying the dusty dignity of a treasured antique. Around it, Meggyesházi Éda sings with poised delicacy, turning each phrase as though testing the joints of language. Dream folk provides a broad shelter for a rigorous study of posture, vulnerability, and the strange politics of inhabiting a body. Éda calls her work “quiet noise,” a useful contradiction for music that gathers force through patience. The trio lets the song unfold by degrees, leaving enough air around each gesture for uncertainty to enter the arrangement. Classical discipline brushes against Patrick Wolf’s theatricality, while Éda’s command of emotional scale carries traces of Anohni, Benjamin Clementine, and Mariam the Believer. Her voice follows an inward geometry, moving from fragile poise towards physical release as it draws on American folk traditions and Celtic song, recalling Mary O’Hara’s Óró Mó Bháidín, later sampled by Passion Pit on Sleepyhead. “Let’s Take Our Bones Out portrays both emotional transformation and the relearning of anatomy,” Éda explains. The premise might sound forbiddingly cerebral, though the track remains sensuous throughout. Its concern with the Alexander Technique gives the song an unusual frame: posture becomes memory, tension becomes biography, and the skeleton turns into a structure open to revision. Éda’s voice bends around these ideas with calm intensity, while the banjo introduces a faintly uncanny domestic texture, homely and estranged at once. Across its measured duration, small changes carry uncommon pressure: a tightened vowel, a pause held open, a banjo note left bare enough to expose its wooden grain and age. Watch the video for Let’s Take Our Bones Out below: Let’s Take Our Bones Out reverses the gaze established by their previous release, Flatland. Previously, a peculiar couple watched the group; now the trio occupies the centre, exposed to scrutiny while retaining an elusive composure. This change suits a song about learning the body again. Observation becomes participation, and anatomy appears as a set of habits waiting to be unlearned. The title carries a childlike gruesomeness, imagining liberation through impossible surgery. Éda treats that image with tenderness, locating freedom in minute acts of awareness away from spectacle. Notes hang with deliberate weight; silences become small rooms where the listener can register breath, muscle and balance. Even the folk materials feel freshly handled, stripped of ornament and placed under curious light. “This song is a moment of reflection: it shows how I began translating my emotions through the language of water,” the band says on their Bandcamp. “Flatland is also a revelation, as it is not our task to control the water, or the ’emotions of the great seas.’ The point isn’t to control any of it, but rather to learn to float within it, to trust it, and to create a sense of kinship with it. The song comes to life through telling stories that carry the elements most essential for me in forming connections or building relationships.” Watch the video for Flatland below: Only Salt, due in September 2026 through Klinik and Corner Art Management, is described as an album about Éda’s relationship with water. Let’s Take Our Bones Out suggests that this relationship will extend beyond symbolism into method: yielding, balancing, adjusting, finding motion through attention. The sacred quality associated with Musica Moralia comes through here without grand ceremony. A modest instrument, a searching voice and a patient structure are enough to make the body feel newly strange, then newly possible. Find Let’s Take Our Bones via streaming here, and listen to Flatland below and order the single here. items.body:
Robert Hood’s minimal techno masterpiece enters orbit again, over 30 years after its initial release.

Originally found on the ‘Internal Empire’ album and also released as a 12” in 1995, the lead cut is an all-too-short piece of whirring Detroit mechanics flecked with icy trills and slinky gear shifts as only he can do. Handily, the 12” offers a slightly extended version with ‘Master Builder (Sandman Option)’ giving it a highly effective nip ’n tuck that gets right under the skin of the dance, while ‘Quartz’ strides out with filtered organ motifs on a whipsmart groove.
items._cn_summary: Robert Hood的极简主义techno经典作品以12寸黑胶形式再版发行，距离1995年原版已逾三十年。主打曲呈现出底特律特有的机械化质感，融合冰冷颤音与流畅的节奏转换，短小精悍却极具辨识度。延伸版本'沙人选项'对原曲进行了更深入的节奏重组，使律动更具渗透力。收录曲'Quartz'以滤波处理的风琴动机为核心，构筑出利落而聪慧的低保真律动。整张作品延续了底特律techno对机械节奏与极简结构的传统探索，发行厂牌为独立地下厂牌，体现出对原始电子音乐美学的坚持。

items.body:
With Aguayo’s Closer Musik classics still fond in the memory - despite more than 25 years having passed! - the chimeric Chilean boss of Cómeme gathers a new squad of international players for ‘Anenoa’, a helplessly diverse testament to his binds with pop, dance, Latin club music, and electronica, and strengths in collaboration, with Etienne Jaumet, Angel Deradoorian, Rafael Cohen (!!!), and Matt Karmil on board...

 

"Matias Aguayo returns with Anenoa, a vibrant and imaginative new album. Known for continually redefining the possibilities of electronic music,  Aguayo’s latest work expands his exploration of voice, rhythm, and collective experience — creating songs that invite participation as much as they reward listening.

Across more than two decades, Aguayo has remained one of the most inventive figures in contemporary electronic music. From co-founding the influential duo Closer Musik, to his long-standing creative relationship with Kompakt, and the creation of the genre-defying C meme label, Aguayo has consistently pushed dance music beyond  convention — blending raw electronics, storytelling, humor, and performance into something deeply human and alive.

Now based in Mexico, Aguayo’s music has absorbed the vibrant energy of community-driven dance culture. Much of Anenoa is sung in Spanish and shaped by a spirit o collaboration that runs throughout the record. Long known for building creative communities through his label and performances, Aguayo brings together a diverse group o artists across Latin America, Europe, and beyond, turning the album into a constellation of voices and perspectives."

items._cn_summary: 智利音乐人 Matias Aguayo 携新专辑回归，延续其在电子舞曲领域二十余年的探索轨迹。专辑以西班牙语演唱为核心，融合拉美俱乐部节奏与电子声响，邀请 Etienne Jaumet、Deradoorian、Matt Karmil 等多位国际音乐人参与合作，呈现出跨越拉丁美洲与欧洲的多元声景。评论指出作品延续了创作者对声音、节奏与集体参与感的关注，强调社区式舞曲文化与协作精神在专辑中的核心地位。整体气质介于舞曲律动与实验探索之间，既保留了俱乐部音乐的感染力，也融入了叙事性与表演性的艺术表达。

items.body:
Bay Area rapper Sha Ray teams up with DJ Haram on her debut album, spitting bold, unapologetic sex raps over Haram's heady but hard-hitting industrial-tinged beats. Heavy duty material FFO Gangsta Boo, Debby Friday or BbyMutha.

Back in 2022, Haram caught Sha Ray on stage in Brooklyn and was immediately struck by her presence. When Sha Ray tapped her for beats later on, she was already sold, meeting again face-to-face at an Armand Hammer/DJ Haram show in Los Angeles not long afterwards. But the collaboration didn't happen in a single studio; 'Critical Thot' is the result of a lengthy period of back-and-forth between Haram in Brooklyn and Sha Ray, who would reply to Haram's beats with demo versions of tracks and notes. As these demos evolved into proper tracks, Haram and Sha Ray's relationship blossomed and 'Critical Thot' emerged - a record that's inspired by both artists' experiences of their role as women in the music industry. 

Haram's grown significantly as a producer in the last few years. Her solo debut 'Beside Myself' was clearly a milestone, but she's also been spotted providing beats for a slew of Backwoodz regulars, from billy woods and Elucid to Ghais Guevara and Fielded. And 'Critical Thot' offers her the scratchpad she needed to try out some of her most adventurous ideas. Sha Ray doesn't stutter on 'The Material' when Haram cuts strings to ribbons over stuttering voices, oscillating from fast to slow, and although she meets Haram's snakelike Memphis groove with similar energy on 'Champagne and Bouquets', she's impressively unfazed when Haram pivots at the midway point, adding fairyale strings and musicbox chimes. 

Oakland rapper Nappy Nina shows up on 'Hey Queen' alongside Brookyln's JWords and both join Sha Ray for an alien-voiced deadpan over one of Haram's most uncompromising beats, a squashed, industrial-tinged speedrun through techno's muckiest edges that'd give Brodinski a run for his money. On 'Strictly', meanwhile, Haram pushes up the tempo to a brisk Jersey bounce and Sha Ray's charisma spills from every rubbery kick. "This is for my bitches, strictly for the bitches," she hisses. There's no doubt.
items._cn_summary: 湾区说唱人Sha Ray与制作人DJ Haram首张全长合作专辑，以大胆直白的性主题说唱为载体，承载两位女性音乐人对行业经验的反思。Haram的工业质感制作成为核心牵引——破碎弦乐采样、蛇形孟菲斯律动、童话音盒铃声交织，在硬朗打击乐与变形人声之间反复切换。从布鲁克林到奥克兰的远程协作模式催生了专辑有机生长的结构，多位女性说唱人参与客串，强化了专辑作为女性群体表达的整体姿态。Haram近年的制作进化在此集中展现，既有保留Backwoodz厂牌地下说唱基因的锋利，又向更实验性的声响美学延展。整张专辑在节奏张力与情绪层次之间维持着罕见的平衡。

items.body:
Described as a "tiny big band", Parasite Jazz are a French non-jazz trio who make heady genre-averse library music from tape loops, found objects and a few carefully picked instruments.

Parasite Jazz materialized in 2023 with their self-titled debut, an introductory set that veered sharply from medieval folk to cartoon trance and space rock. But they've developed significantly since then; after touring France for a few months, they've matured and grown into their roles, shifting away from carnivalesque abstraction towards dark, lounge-y exotica. It's the kind of gear that's hard to place: are we hearing samples, or is it a live band? Tamara Goukassova leads on violin, synth, ocarina, voice and objects, while Alexandre Larcier handles the samples and tape loops and Théo Delaunay makes up the rhythm section. And although 'Apocalypse (Egged Up)' sounds like a hold tone rendition of the 'Twin Peaks' love theme, the lengthy 'Mascara' is more like an electro samba improv jam, while 'Black Moon' sounds like Tortoise jamming with Jean-Claude Vannier. Not bad at all.
items._cn_summary: 法国三人组合 Parasite Jazz 在第二张专辑中完成了显著的成长与转型。乐队自称「迷你大乐队」，以磁带循环、拾得物件和少量精选乐器构建出拒绝被归类的库藏音乐（library music）声响。较之首张作品在中古民谣、卡通 trance 与太空摇滚间的游走，本作明显朝暗色调的 lounge 异国爵士方向沉淀，呈现出难以分辨是采样还是现场演奏的模糊质感。Tamara Goukassova 负责小提琴、合成器、陶笛与人声采样，Alexandre Larcier 操控采样与磁带循环，Théo Delaunay 担纲节奏段落。'Apocalypse (Egged Up)' 带有《双峰》恋曲主题的延续气质，'Mascara' 展开为电子 samba 即兴，'Black Moon' 则让人联想到 Tortoise 与 Jean-Claude Vannier 的即兴碰撞。整体文本信息量适中，源自独立小众平台 Boomkat，具有一定跨类型融合价值。

items.body:
Antwerp’s ace Cortizona label task Jlin, The Hafler Trio, Ossia, Legowelt, Peaking Lights and many more to rework the dry machine action of Belgian mainstay Walter Verdin.

Not even the best track on his ‘PingPong’ 2LP - that would be either ‘Aceton’ or ‘Sequence X’ - ‘Minimalise’ is nevertheless characteristic of Walter Verdin’s near-half century of synth pursuits that once saw him as part of Belgium’s 1983 Eur*vision entry, with Pas De Deux. Thus the track’s arid paucity of ingredients, of vox, bleep track and white noise, supplies mutable material for the remixers, who generally hew faithful to his asceticism and drily Belgian wits on another screwball set from the guess-again label, Cortizona.

The most impressive is Jlin’s propulsive future footwork take, fizzing with concentrated details and prone to wickedly wrong-foot the ‘floor in its ride intricacies, whilst The Hafler Trio play true to form and the track title with a curiously compressed and smeared slant on the same elements that uncannily gets under skin. Closer to home, Sagat emphasises a certain Lowlands gloom with a tense type of deconstructed D&B restraint, resolving in mutant offbeats, and Legowelt does his ‘80s sci-fi thing with vocoders and 808 halfstep.

Elsewhere Peaking Lights’ the Verdin to the ‘floor with a coldwave house reduction, Beton Brut puckers it up like one of Mumdnce & Logoos’ weightless ping jobs, DJ Marcelle does her freeform noise punk thing, replete with typical snip of The Fall, and Annelies Monseré lathers its lyrics into a mantric sound poem.
items._genre: experimental electronic / IDM / minimal synth / coldwave / industrial
items._cn_summary: 比利时厂牌Cortizona邀请多位实验电子音乐人重新解构Walter Verdin的简约合成器原作。Jlin以未来footwork节奏驱动，细节密布，节拍结构诡谲；The Hafler Trio延续压缩涂抹式的极简手法；Sagat以低地国家式的阴沉气质融入解构D&B节奏；Legowelt带来80年代科幻感的vocoder与808半速节拍。Peaking Lights将原作压缩为冷波浩室，Beton Brut效仿Mumdance & Logos的失重质感，DJ Marcelle以自由噪音朋克手法加入The Fall的碎片采样，Annelies Monseré则将歌词转化为冥想式的声诗。整张合辑忠于原作的极简与干涩美学，多种实验电子路径并存，展现比利时地下电子场景的多元创造力。

items.body:
Swiss unarchivers WRWTFWW give vinyl wings to a cult, 1999 Japan suite of jazz-spurred techno and shine-eyed electronica balanced between Warp’s AI comps and A.R.T.’s future jazz styles

“Sarah's, Satins and Blades (The Way We Found Each Other) is a limited-edition cassette currently presented as part of Lemons, Laws & Secret Doors: A Hastings Queer History Collective Exhibition at
items.body:
In a blend of concrète collage and spoken word, Osàre! Editions boss Elena Colombi hails Hastings’ heritage of refusenik queer counter-culture with a richly informative, playfully witty, and fascinating mixtape appropriate to the collective’s analog newsletter medium and underground dissemination...

“Sarah's, Satins and Blades (The Way We Found Each Other) is a limited-edition cassette currently presented as part of Lemons, Laws & Secret Doors: A Hastings Queer History Collective Exhibition at Hastings Museum. Drawing on newsletters produced by the Campaign for Homosexual Equality Hastings Group (CHASTE) and the 1066 Gay Community Organisation between 1974 and 1989, the work is presented on a medium contemporary to these publications, echoing the routes they once travelled: from room to room, hand to hand.

The A-side brings together readings from the original newsletters, reflections from members of the Hastings Queer History Collective, and fragments of fast-changing music. Announcements, advice columns and calls to action sit alongside personal testimony, tracing how queer people lived, met, organised and communicated across generations.

Expanding beyond the exhibition, the cassette lingers in voice as a space of memory, exchange and connection. As both object and document, it proposes an archive that can move again: rewound, replayed and passed on through new networks of listening. Following the exhibition, the cassette will also enter Hastings Museum's permanent collection.

The B-side features a composition developed during a residency at Piedicavallo Festival, Italy. Written during a difficult period, it reflects on care, friendship, recovery and connection, offering a fitting coda to a work centred on queer resilience and collective memory.”
items._genre: concrète / spoken word / experimental collage / electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张限量版磁带是Elena Colombi与Hastings酷儿历史集体合作的成果，以具体音乐拼贴与口语朗读为核心媒介。A面汇集1974至1989年间当地同性恋平等运动通讯的原始文本、集体成员反思以及快速变化的音乐碎片，公告、建议专栏与行动号召与个人证词交织，追溯酷儿群体几代人在聚会、组织与沟通中的方式。B面则是她在意大利Piedicavallo音乐节驻留期间创作的一首作品，聚焦关怀、友谊与重建连接。整张作品不仅作为展览的伴生物存在，也将进入Hastings博物馆永久收藏。卡带作为实体媒介的选择，呼应了当年通讯在手中传递的地下网络，使档案重新获得流动性与可听性。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online.
